entries.title: #714.Tibo 谈 Codex：harness 总比模型快一步
entries.content:
📝 本期播客简介

本期我们克隆了：The Pragmatic Engineer · Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

原内容更新时间：2026-09-09

本期节目邀请 Codex 创始团队成员、现任 OpenAI Core Products & Platform 负责人 Tibo，回顾 Codex 从内部研究项目走向产品的过程。对谈从 Tibo 在谷歌和 DeepMind 的经历开始，聊到他为何加入 OpenAI，以及早期 ASWE 项目如何逐渐发展为 Codex。

节目重点拆解了 Codex 的工程选择：为什么核心 Agent 使用 Rust 编写，为什么 Codex CLI、SDK 和应用服务器选择开源，以及为什么 Codex 不绑定 OpenAI 的模型。Tibo 也解释了 harness 如何为模型提供安全、可靠和高效的“拐杖”，以及模型能力增强后，harness 为什么会逐渐变薄。

后半部分聚焦 AI 如何改变软件工程的完整生命周期：自动化 code review、安全检查、依赖升级和架构重构，维护成本下降后会带来怎样的工程变化，以及 Codex 如何融入 OpenAI 内部的文档、Slack、代码库和新人入职流程。节目还深入讨论了 Codex 与 ChatGPT 合并时的系统挑战，以及 Tibo 如何用 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 管理日常工作。

👤 本期嘉宾

Tibo 是 Codex 早期创建者之一，Codex 作为产品刚起步时便参与其中，此后持续带领 Codex 团队。目前他负责 OpenAI 的 Core Products & Platform 组织，该组织也包括 Codex。

在加入 OpenAI 之前，Tibo 曾在谷歌和 DeepMind 工作。他在谷歌参与过提升移动端网络速度的项目，后来加入谷歌地图团队，负责评价系统；在 DeepMind 期间，他长期从事研究基础设施和研究工具建设，也参与过早期大语言模型对话系统的内部探索。Tibo 的经历横跨应用数学、创业、研究基础设施、模型和产品工程，因此能从工程、研究和产品协同的角度解释 Codex 是如何被构建出来的。

⏱️ 时间戳

00:48 从乡村电脑到OpenAI

06:13 从DeepMind对话到OpenAI

11:31 Codex为何用Rust开源

20:10 开放模型与云端执行

27:09 Harness如何推动软件工程

48:52 Codex合并ChatGPT后的未来

🌟 精彩内容

💡 harness 总是比模型领先一步

harness 的作用不是替代模型，而是通过护栏、工具、developer message 和执行环境，让模型已有的能力变得更可靠、更高效、更符合用户预期。随着模型本身变强，原本必须写在 harness 里的引导逻辑会逐渐减少。

"harness 总是比模型稍微领先一点。"

💡 Rust 是 Agent 与产品之间的边界

Codex 选择 Rust，并不只是为了性能，而是为了让 Agent 核心拥有更强的正确性、安全性和可扩展性。将 Agent 与产品清晰隔离，也能避免两者过度耦合，为后续创新留下空间。

"但把 Agent 本身和产品清晰地隔离开，让它脱离产品也能独立存在，这是一个非常重要的原则。"

💡 开源是为了参与正在变化的社区

Codex 开源不仅是为了获得贡献，也因为代码 Agent 正在改变代码本身的作用。OpenAI 希望亲自进入这个社区，直接体验开发者遇到的问题，同时让外部开发者共同探索优秀 harness 应该是什么样子。

"如果我们真能做成功，开源本身会改变，代码本身的作用也会改变，所以身处这个社区之中显得很重要，而不是跟它脱节。"

💡 靠真本事赢，而不是靠模型绑定

Codex 支持多个模型提供商，既减少用户为了尝试新模型而更换整套工具的成本，也迫使团队同时在模型、harness、产品体验和开源生态上保持竞争力。

"我喜欢靠真本事去赢，而不是靠绑定去赢。"

💡 code review 正从代码审查变成意图讨论

正确性、安全性和复杂依赖关系的检查，越来越可以由 Agent 自动完成。人类更重要的工作，可能转向讨论功能是否值得做、架构意图是否正确，以及团队是否对系统必须满足的不变式达成共识。

"我觉得这种讨论完全可以在 PR 之外进行。没必要非得围着代码聊。"

💡 维护成本下降，重构和犯错会变得更便宜

依赖升级、安全补丁和大规模代码修改，未来可能被 Agent 自动完成。由于重构成本降低，团队可以更频繁地调整架构，但抽象、边界和不变式仍然重要，它们决定了系统能否快速变化而不影响其他部分。

"所以犯错的成本，我认为是在下降的。"

💡 软件的生命周期正在被压缩

过去一个系统从小团队逐渐扩展到大型工程，需要较长时间来补齐文档、流程和架构；现在，Agent 可能在一个周末就让大量代码同时进入系统，工程团队必须更早考虑边界、维护和协作方式。

"现在就像突然爆发一样，一下子就有 100 个 Agent 在给这套东西做贡献。"

💡 最重要的能力是快速理解和持续追问

Tibo 给想进入 Codex、OpenAI 或 AI 初创公司的工程师的建议，不是只熟练使用工具，而是保持对系统运作方式的好奇心，快速读懂新代码库，并通过不断追问“五个为什么”建立清晰理解。

"我觉得有两件事很重要，一是对事物运作方式抱有极深极深的好奇心，二是能训练自己非常快速地理解事物的能力。"

🌐 播客信息补充

本播客采用原有人声声线进行播客音频制作，也可能会有一些地方听起来怪怪的

使用 AI 进行翻译，因此可能会有一些地方不通顺

entries.title: NASA’s Chandra Unveils Mysterious X-Ray Objects
entries.content:
[![Researchers found 84 so-called hypersoft X-ray sources in M101, Messier 31, and four elliptical galaxies. This newly-discovered class of objects give off very low-energy X-rays and likely high levels of ultraviolet light. Their existence may help explain questions around Type Ia supernova explosions and the intergalactic medium. These images of the face-on spiral galaxy M101 show X-ray data from Chandra and an optical image from the Hubble Space Telescope.](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/missions/chandra/2026/m101.jpg?w=8999&h=9011&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/missions/chandra/2026/m101.jpg?w=8999&h=9011&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)

X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Alabama/M. Muhibullah et al.; Optical: NASA/ESA/STScI; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/N. Wolk

Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, scientists have discovered a new class of objects behaving unlike any they have seen before. Astronomers suggest these newly spotted objects in other galaxies may help solve not one, but two long-standing questions in astrophysics.

These mysterious objects give off unusually low-energy X-rays but intense levels of ultraviolet radiation. This discovery is featured in a paper published Wednesday in Nature Astronomy.

“We’ve never encountered a group of objects that act like this,” said ﻿Mustafa Muhibullah of the University of Alabama who led the study. “Of course, the next step was to try to figure out what these things are.”

[![Researchers found 84 so-called hypersoft X-ray sources in M101, Messier 31, and four elliptical galaxies. This newly-discovered class of objects give off very low-energy X-rays and likely high levels of ultraviolet light. Their existence may help explain questions around Type Ia supernova explosions and the intergalactic medium. These images of the face-on spiral galaxy M101 show X-ray data from Chandra and an optical image from the Hubble Space Telescope.](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/missions/chandra/2026/m101_labeled.jpg?w=8999&h=9011&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/missions/chandra/2026/m101_labeled.jpg?w=8999&h=9011&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)

M101 with illustrated circles calling out seven of the newly-discovered objects.

X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Alabama/M. Muhibullah et al.; Optical: NASA/ESA/STScI; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/N. Wolk

The researchers found a total of 84 of these “hypersoft X-ray sources” – so named because they give such low-energy X-rays – in the six different galaxies they searched, using data openly available to the public in the Chandra archive. Two of the galaxies are spirals, M31 (the Andromeda galaxy) and M101 (the Pinwheel galaxy), while the other four are ellipticals. They found hypersoft X-ray sources both in regions of active star formation and areas where there are older stars.

The team spotted the sources by finding objects that appeared in Chandra images taken at the lowest X-ray energies but vanished in higher-energy images. That means these objects give off far more low-energy X-rays than high-energy ones. Because low-energy X-rays border energetic ultraviolet radiation on the electromagnetic spectrum, the researchers determined that these sources are producing large amounts of energetic ultraviolet radiation as well.

It is unclear what types of objects are responsible for these low-energy X-rays and intense ultraviolet radiation. The team thinks they most likely involve a black hole, neutron star, or white dwarf pulling material from a companion star. The material pulled from the companion star is heated up to produce X-rays before falling onto the white dwarf or neutron star, or into the black hole. Such binary systems have been seen before, but not with such bright ultraviolet radiation and low-energy X-rays.

The discovery suggests that there may be large populations of binary systems with energetic ultraviolet radiation that have been undetected until now.

“These clandestine X-ray sources are actually among the most energetic objects in galaxies, and they could be solving two cosmic mysteries at once,” said Muhibullah.

Scientists think that some white dwarf systems pulling material from companion stars may eventually explode as a supernova – known as a Type Ia – that is critical for measuring the expansion of the universe. These supernovae played a key role in discovering that this expansion is accelerating. Astronomers have been looking for the stars that turn into Type Ia supernovae for many years, so far without success.

“If we could find a way to spot these Type Ia supernova explosions before they go off, that would be really important,” said co-author Jimmy Irwin, also of the University of Alabama. “Right now, we study them after they’ve exploded, and astronomers have struggled to understand what is actually ignited.”

The other mystery these hypersoft X-ray sources might explain is what strips electrons from gas between the stars in some galaxies. This stripping of electrons is important to probe because it can affect how quickly stars form and influence the life cycles of galaxies. Hot, massive stars play a role, but they do not completely explain what is causing this stripping. The intense levels of ultraviolet radiation from the hypersoft X-ray sources may play a vital role.

Why were these hypersoft X-ray sources not found until now? In addition to the low-energy X-ray output, which is very difficult for X-ray telescopes to detect, the high-energy ultraviolet radiation is readily absorbed by helium and hydrogen gas that fills the space between the stars, creating a nearly impenetrable barrier to look through.

“By combing through the Chandra archive, we were able to eliminate what used to be a blind spot for telescopes,” said co-author Rosanne Di Stefano of the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian. “That’s how we found what appears to be a new class of cosmic objects with remarkable qualities.”

NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, manages the Chandra program. The Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory’s Chandra X-ray Center controls science operations from Cambridge, Massachusetts, and flight operations from Burlington, Massachusetts.

[Read more from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory](https://chandra.si.edu/photo/2026/m101/)

To learn more about NASA’s Chandra mission, visit:

<https://www.nasa.gov/chandra>

## **Visual Description**

This release features a composite image of a spiral galaxy, M101; one of six identified galaxies housing a new class of mysterious objects that give off unusually low-energy X-rays.

In this composite image, M101 faces us directly. It has multiple arms in shades of purple, spiraling clockwise around a golden yellow core. Scattered along and between the arms are scores of tiny specks in white and purple. Most of those specks are pairs of stars, but seven of them are a mystery.

To casual observers, the unusual objects are visually indistinguishable from the other specks of light in the galaxy. An annotated version of the composite image is included in this release, with red circles around the mysterious specks for easy identification.

These mystery specks behave like no other class of object discovered before. The curious objects give off X-rays of such low energy, they in fact produce large amounts of ultraviolet radiation, as UV radiation borders X-rays on the electromagnetic spectrum. Searching images of galaxies with low-energy X-rays in the Chandra Observatory archive, scientists have found a total of 84 such objects spread across M101 and five other galaxies. They have dubbed these mysterious objects “hypersoft X-ray sources.”

entries.title: Five‑metal alloy: Scientists create ultra‑stable catalyst for fuel cells
entries.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
entries.content: Hydrogen-powered cars, power stations and portable chargers all rely on fuel cells. At the heart of each fuel cell is a catalyst that speeds up the reaction between hydrogen and oxygen to produce electricity and water. These catalysts are typically made of platinum—which costs nearly as much as gold. Researchers from Southern Federal University, together with colleagues from Skoltech (part of the VEB.RF Group), the Institute of Catalysis of the Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, and Bauman Moscow State Technical University, have found a way to make this key component both cheaper and better. They developed a catalyst from a five-metal alloy that retains its activity even after 10,000 operating cycles.

entries.title: Apple just made the iPhone 17 lineup $100 more expensive
entries.content:
Alongside the $1,999 iPhone Duo price, Apple has also increased the price of every older model it still sells including the aging [iPhone 16](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone-16 "iPhone 16") by $100 as ongoing component shortages continue to bite.  
  

![Black iPhone with dual rear cameras leaning against a light gray textured wall, standing on a wooden surface](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/68507-144367-iPhone-17-xl.jpg)  
The iPhone 17 just got more expensive

  
Apple's big [iPhone](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone "iPhone") event saw the company unveil the [iPhone 18 Pro](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone-18 "iPhone 18"), iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. But no mention was made as to the fate of the existing models in the iPhone lineup.  
  
However, following the return of Apple's online store, we now know that all existing models haven't escaped the price hikes. Apple previously [increased prices](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/06/25/apple-confirms-price-nikes-across-macs-ipads-and-more) on its [iPad](https://appleinsider.com/inside/ipad "iPad") and [Mac](https://appleinsider.com/inside/mac "Mac") lineups in June 2026.

entries.title: Google is a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Enterprise AI Assistants
entries.content:
We are excited to share that Gartner has named Google a Leader in its inaugural [2026 Magic Quadrant for Enterprise AI Assistants](https://cloud.google.com/resources/content/2026-gartner-magic-quadrant-enterprise-ai-assistants). In this comprehensive evaluation of top enterprise AI assistant vendors, Gartner placed Google in the Leaders quadrant for its evaluation across both Completeness of Vision and Ability to Execute.

Gemini Enterprise helps organizations bring helpful, secure AI directly into the daily work of their employees. It moves teams past basic chat interactions to automating multi-step, end-to-end workflows with AI agents. It connects with the tools and infrastructure companies already use and scales easily and cost-effectively, all with security and governance in place. 

We see this recognition from Gartner as validation of our goal: creating a unified platform where everyone — from business users to developers — can work alongside AI agents to accomplish more together.

### Our take on Google as a Leader

Amid a complex landscape of standalone AI tools and emerging platforms, Gemini Enterprise emerges as a unified, open agentic platform backed by Google’s full AI stack, with strengths mentioned in the report such as:

* **Unified “AI front door”**: Gemini Enterprise unifies enterprise chat and search, first and third-party agents, a no-code agent designer, Google Workspace integration, and third-party connectors all in one platform, eliminating the need for organizations to piece together disparate AI tools.
* **Open connectivity:** Gemini Enterprise offers extensive connectivity beyond Google's ecosystem — extending to Microsoft 365, other third-party software, and internal enterprise data sources. This open connectivity lets organizations adopt Gemini Enterprise alongside their existing infrastructure without costly system overhauls.
* **Simple economics:** Gemini Enterprise offers a straightforward pricing model, with actions like chat and search included in the base SKU. Organizations can select per-user seat subscriptions, as well as a pay-as-you-go option that lets users run agent workloads without hitting quota limits mid-task.
* **Built-in governance:** Gemini Enterprise provides robust agent governance out-of-the- box at no extra cost, enabling enterprises to seamlessly manage users, agents, and data permissions while curbing security risks and agent sprawl.
* **Full-stack depth and scale**: Google’s vertically-integrated stack provides global infrastructure, custom silicon, world-class models, and a secure, enterprise-ready foundation — all optimized for security, interoperability, and cost.

To read the full report, download it [here](https://cloud.google.com/resources/content/2026-gartner-magic-quadrant-enterprise-ai-assistants).

* **FinOps and cost controls:** [New FinOps and cost-control capabilities](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/flexible-billing-and-cost-controls-for-agents-on-google-cloud?e=48754805) were introduced last month, allowing organizations to optimize AI spend through more pricing options, Flexible Savings Plans, and granular spend management.

### Gemini Enterprise customers are also seeing the value

Check out what our customers are saying about the recent product advancements.

entries.title: We Finally Know iOS 27's Release Date
entries.content:
Apple's September event was a big one. The company announced [the new iPhone 18 Pro](https://lifehacker.com/tech/apple-iphone-18-pro-and-iphone-18-pro-max-announcement), Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, AirPods 5, and [the foldable iPhone Duo](https://lifehacker.com/tech/apple-just-announced-the-foldable-iphone-duo). While the company certainly highlighted numerous software features for each of these devices, including some never-before-seen [health features for Apple Watch](https://lifehacker.com/health/apple-health-app-redesign), this was very much a hardware event. That's no surprise, of course: Apple reserves the vast majority of its software news for WWDC in June. But despite that fact, there was one particularly big piece of software news to come out of September's keynote: [iOS 27's](https://lifehacker.com/tech/10-hacks-every-ios-27-user-should-know) release date.

Since Apple is using iOS 27 to advertise many of the capabilities of its upcoming devices, it makes sense that the company would need to give an ETA for the update. After all, the iPhone 18 Pro launches on Friday, Sept. 18, running iOS 27. The update would presumably need to be out by then, unless Apple intended iPhone 18 Pro users to be the first of its user base to run the software. (Spoilers: it did not intend that.)

As it happens, the company officially announced the update's launch date, though it didn't advertise it heavily. At the bottom of its newsroom posts for each of its new product announcements, the company confirmed that iOS 27 will launch on Monday, Sept. 14. Developers have been beta testing iOS 27 since June, and [Apple opened up the public beta one month later](https://lifehacker.com/tech/how-to-install-the-ios-27-public-beta-why-you-probably-shouldnt). Since then, volunteers have been trialing Apple's upcoming features, including Siri AI, new image editing tools, and dual-capture during FaceTime calls.

Apple also confirmed that watchOS 27 will launch on Sept. 14 as well. However, at this time, it isn't clear whether Apple's other software updates, such as macOS 27 Golden Gate and iPadOS 27, will also launch at this time. If I had to guess, I would say these updates will arrive in tandem, especially iPadOS 27, but we'll have to wait for Apple's confirmation to know for sure.

## Which iPhones are compatible with iOS 27?

Apple is supporting a long list of iPhones with iOS 27, going all the way back to 2019's iPhone 11 series. The full list is as follows:

* iPhone Duo
* iPhone 18 Pro
* iPhone 18 Pro Max
* iPhone 17e
* iPhone 17
* iPhone 17 Pro
* iPhone 17 Pro Max
* iPhone Air
* iPhone 16e
* iPhone 16
* iPhone 16 Plus
* iPhone 16 Pro
* iPhone 16 Pro Max
* iPhone 15
* iPhone 15 Plus
* iPhone 15 Pro
* iPhone 15 Pro Max
* iPhone 14
* iPhone 14 Plus
* iPhone 14 Pro
* iPhone 14 Pro Max
* iPhone 13
* iPhone 13 mini
* iPhone 13 Pro
* iPhone 13 Pro Max
* iPhone 12
* iPhone 12 mini
* iPhone 12 Pro
* iPhone 12 Pro Max
* iPhone 11
* iPhone 11 Pro
* iPhone 11 Pro Max
* iPhone SE (2nd generation and later)

That said, some features are only available on certain iPhone models. Apple Intelligence (including Siri AI) is only accessible on iPhone 15 Pro and newer. Certain AI features, like Siri voice customization, is only available on iPhone 17 Pro and newer, including iPhone Air.

entries.title: Why the Apple Health App's Redesign Is a Big Deal
entries.content:
We may earn a commission from links on this page.

Apple announced new watches today—a [Series 12](https://zdcs.link/QqOY4q?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Series%2012&object_type=content&short_url=QqOY4q&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") and an Ultra 4—which you [can read more about here](https://www.cnet.com/news-live/apple-event-2026-live-updates/ "open in a new window"). But alongside the watch features, Apple announced a revamped Health app. We’ll soon have a proper dashboard for health data and insights, rivaling what you can get from the companion apps for other wearables like Whoop, Garmin, and Fitbit.

[Apple Watch Series 12

Pre-order Here

![Apple Watches, Series 12](https://lifehacker.com/imagery/articles/01M23QABFDVB45NXCTC30FM6K9/images-1.fill.size_autoxauto.v1788979549.png)

![Apple Watches, Series 12](https://lifehacker.com/imagery/articles/01M23QABFDVB45NXCTC30FM6K9/images-1.fill.size_autoxauto.v1788979549.png)

Pre-order Here](https://cc.lifehacker.com/v1/otc/06ZVRiLmglGs4QA6plTXzTC?url=https%3A%2F%2Fzdcs.link%2FQqOY4q&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=offer-btn&position=1&element_label=Apple+Watch+Series+12&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss&short_code=https%3A%2F%2Fzdcs.link%2FQqOY4q&object_type=article&object_uuid=01M23QABFDVB45NXCTC30FM6K9&pageview_type=RSS "(opens in a new window)")

## Why Apple needed a better health dashboard

Apple was an early trendsetter when it came to health-focused watches, but it quickly fell behind as all the other devices began adding sleep scores, recovery scores, and customized insights based on your day’s data. If you open up a good wearable app, you’ll instantly know what’s going on with your body’s data and what you should probably do about it. I’m often skeptical of the specifics—you [shouldn’t read too much into any app’s metrics](https://lifehacker.com/health/the-data-you-can-and-cant-trust-from-fitness-wearables)—but it’s good to have *something* to look at.

The Apple Health app has existed for years, but it’s mostly a dry listing of data from different sources. Which is a shame, because it has access to an incredible amount of data, not to mention [powerful hidden features](https://lifehacker.com/health/best-apple-health-hacks) that most of us never manage to discover.

Last year, Apple [finally revamped its Fitness app](https://lifehacker.com/health/ios-26-gives-the-iphone-a-real-fitness-app) to match what other wearables give us in terms of activity tracking. This year, we finally get the other half: a Health app that can tell you how well you slept, how “recovered” you are, and how your long-term health seems to be shaping up.

## What’s coming to the redesigned Health app

Although Apple showed these features in the context of an Apple Watch upgrade (more on that below), the things that intrigue me most are likely to be software updates that roll out to iPhones in general. That’s my guess, in any case—I’ll watch Apple’s announcements for more details as they become available.

Apple showed a new Readiness score, which can tell you whether you need to “recover,” should “pace yourself,” are “ready,” or should “go for it.” (That’s in order from worst to best.) This score can update during the day, making it a more readable version of something like Garmin’s Body Battery.

When you open your Health app, it looks like relevant “insights” will show up at the top of the screen, including your sleep, recovery, and rings, and the main screen can show your sleep from the past night along with a sleep score. The app includes text summaries and guidance that are generated by Apple Intelligence, suggesting that you'll need an iPhone 16 or later for these.

In the screenshots Apple shared, I spied a tiny number that is actually a huge change of focus for the company: one of the insights shows your rings next to your step count for the day. Apple has never made a big deal about steps, to the point where people often download third-party step counters to be able to easily view steps on the watch. But the Health app has kept count all along, and now that number is showing up somewhere you can easily see it.

Depending on how well Apple executes this idea, I could see apps like [Bevel](https://lifehacker.com/health/bevel-apple-watch-app-review) becoming obsolete. And Bevel already makes some wearables’ apps (like Google Health) obsolete—you can just read the data from Bevel, or now Apple Health, instead of using the app that comes with your Fitbit. Other fitness tech companies will now have a serious competitor that is available for free on customers’ phones.

## Longevity and VO2max assessments are another big change

I roll my eyes every time a health or fitness app claims to gauge my “longevity” or some true “age” of my body. Depending on which app you ask, I’m either 10 years younger than I really am, or three years older.

Apple has joined the club, with a whole Longevity tab in the Health app. (That now brings the number of tabs to three: the main screen, the sharing tab, and now longevity in the middle.) Despite the eye-rolling, I see what Apple is doing here. Don’t think of longevity in this (or any) app as being an accurate gauge of how long you will live; think of it as how your long-term health habits are adding up. Apple’s longevity calculations involve seven areas, with icons indicating something like nutrition, exercise, heart health, hearing health, movement (maybe steps), sleep, and mental well-being.

There’s also a new set of assessments, including a VO2max assessment. According to Apple’s presentation, you’ll prop your phone up where it can see your full body, and then you’ll step to a metronome’s beat, speeding up as the beeps speed up until you’re running in place. This sounds like it may have been inspired by the [Harvard step test](https://www.physio-pedia.com/Harvard_Step_Test "open in a new window"), which has you step up and down in place and then measure your heart rate. Until now, Apple’s VO2max estimates have always been based on GPS-tracked activities like outdoor running. (Apple finished in the middle of the pack when I [tested the accuracy of nine devices’ VO2max estimates](https://lifehacker.com/health/tested-vo2max-compared-to-fitness-wearables). I’m curious to see whether the new assessment does better.)

## The Apple Watch boasts the “most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable”

When it comes to the full experience—with the Apple Watch itself—there’s a notable upgrade to the Series 12 Apple Watch compared to previous versions. Apple has redesigned the heart rate sensor on the back of the watch, with larger lights and redesigned photodiodes to detect the reflected light.

With these redesigns, Apple says it has the “most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable.” To which I say: I’ll believe it when I see it. In my testing over the past few years, Apple Watches have lagged well behind other wearables’ heart rate sensors when I test them for accuracy. I’d certainly believe that it found room for improvement, but is the new Apple sensor really going to be able to beat Garmin’s fifth-generation sensor, the one that [made me do a double take](https://lifehacker.com/health/garmin-forerunner-570-review) because I thought I had it mixed up with my chest strap data?

Apple [has released a whitepaper](https://www.apple.com/legal/more-resources/docs/Heart_Rate_Accuracy_Study_2026.pdf "open in a new window") with the results of an internal heart rate accuracy study it did comparing the Series 12 (but not the Ultra 4) against the Garmin Forerunner 970, Google Pixel Watch 4, Huawei Watch 5, Samsung Galaxy Watch 8, Whoop 5.0, and Oura Ring 5, with a Polar H10 chest strap for reference. It's a short paper, and doesn't show the kind of detail I would like to see from a thorough test, so you can bet I'll be investigating this myself once I get my hands on the new watch. If Apple really reaches a Forerunner 970 level of accuracy, I’ll be incredibly impressed.

entries.title: Apple's 'Reference Image' Preserves Your Original Photos (Even After You Edit Them)
entries.content:
Figuring out what’s real online is only getting harder, and [AI watermarks](https://lifehacker.com/tech/how-does-ai-watermarking-work-and-how-can-i-check-for-one) can only go so far to identify fakes. But today, Apple introduced a new standard to at least help identify real images taken directly on an iPhone: Apple Reference Image. It won’t solve the problem of finding the truth online, but it could be a helpful tool towards that goal.

The new feature will be available on iPhone 18 Pro models to start. It works by taking signed sensor data from the camera and using it to create a reference picture that can’t be edited, alongside a version that can be changed. The idea here is to give you a version of the picture that’s authenticated at the moment of capture, which you can compare against any modified versions later.

![iPhone camera roll, with a button reading "See Reference Image" to compare original photo.](https://lifehacker.com/imagery/articles/01M23QCDM95SKW35CDNP505RRQ/images-1.fill.size_2000x1125.v1788979066.png)

Credit: Credit: Apple

This provenance metadata can be preserved through certain supported sharing methods, which for now means select other Apple devices can check their verification status. That doesn’t mean that *anyone* can check the veracity of an image—especially if the version that gets posted and shared is an edited variant—but it provides a tool for the person or organization that took the picture originally to offer proof of verification.

This tool comes alongside the announcement that Apple will soon add support for the SynthID standard. This will potentially help users identify when an image has been created or modified with AI. Apple joins a long (though not exactly comprehensive) list of major tech companies to support the standard, including OpenAI, Nvidia, and obviously Google, the original creator of SynthID.

We’re still in the midst of a scattershot image verification ecosystem. Apple’s Reference Image is a clever implementation that gives the end user a signed original to compare a picture against, which is a step up from C2PA metadata that merely embeds information about an image’s origin. It’s still unclear how widely these verification tools will be implemented and how easy it will be for users to trace where an image comes from and how, precisely, it was modified, but still, something is better than nothing.

entries.title: 5 really cool things about the new AirPods 5
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

Apple introduced the AirPods 5 during its [Surprise and Shine event](https://www.macworld.com/article/3228054/surprise-and-shine-apple-event-live-blog-iphone-18-pro-folding-duo-airpods.html) on Wednesday. Apple’s popular earphones have a very similar design to the model they replace, but they feature several internal improvements over the AirPods 4. Here are five things you need to know about the new AirPods 5.

## 1. Better Active Noise Cancellation

Apple introduced Active Noise Cancellation to the entry-level AirPods with the [AirPods 4](https://www.macworld.com/article/2463401/airpods-4-with-anc-review.html) in 2024, a welcome feature for anyone who prefers open-air earphones instead of in-ear ones such as the AirPods Pro. On the AirPods 5, the ANC has gotten even better, thanks to a “new multi-port acoustic architecture and improved computational audio algorithms.” Apple claims that the AirPods 5 removes up to 50 percent more noise compared to the AirPods 4.

Apple also improved Transparency mode so that voices and sounds are more natural. The Adaptive Audio feature tracks the sound in your environment and automatically switches between ANC and Transparency modes.

## 2. Active Noise Cancellation is now standard

Active Noise Cancellation is now a standard feature for the AirPods, meaning you can’t get a model without it, as was the case with AirPods 4. So you no longer have to shop and ponder if you really need ANC or not–if you don’t want to use it, then simply turn it off.

## 3. Improved sound quality

That new multiport acoustic architecture that improved ANC also works with a “next-generation Adaptive EQ” to generate better sound across “an even wider range of ear geometries,” according to Apple’s announcement. This also makes Personalized Spatial Audio sound more immersive.

![AirPods 5](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/airpods-5-1.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple made improvements that result in better sound from the AirPods 5.

Apple

## 4. Better battery life

The AirPods 5 are rated at 5 hours of playback with ANC active, which is one hour longer than the AirPods 4. Combined with the charging case, the AirPods 5 offer 22 hours of battery life when using ANC, a two-hour boost over the AirPods 4.

## 5. The price

The AirPods 5 with a USB-C charging case is $129, which is the same as the AirPods 4 *without* ANC, effectively a $50 price cut over AirPods 4 with ANC. In this [era of increasing prices](https://www.macworld.com/article/3229342/iphone-price-increases.html), this is a great surprise.

One caveat, however. The $129 AirPods now come with a wired charging case, which means you need to plug it in to charge it. If that’s a nuisance, Apple offers the AirPods 5 with a wireless charging case for $149 (and you’ll also get volume controls built into the stems like AirPods Pro). So, the AirPods 5 (with ANC standard) and the wireless charging case are still $30 cheaper than the AirPods 4 with ANC. Cool.

The AirPods 5 are available for pre-order now, with shipments starting on September 18.

entries.title: iPhone 18 Pro & Max Guide: Everything you need to know about the new iPhones
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

Apple has unveiled the **iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max**. They retain the 6.3-inch and 6.9-inch screen sizes and aluminium unibody design introduced with the previous generation, but Apple has made substantial changes to the cameras, processor, cooling, battery life and connectivity.

The biggest camera upgrade is a new **48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture**, which can automatically move between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8 and ƒ/4 depending on lighting and depth of field. Apple says the widest aperture delivers around **50% better low-light performance**, while new Pro controls add manual aperture, shutter speed, white balance and histogram controls.

Inside is the **A20 Pro**, Apple’s first iPhone chip made using a 2nm process. It has a new six-core CPU, seven-core GPU, Dual 16-core Neural Engine and 50% more memory bandwidth than the A19 Pro. A larger vapor chamber and new M-series-inspired chip packaging also improve heat dissipation, with Apple claiming up to **40% better sustained performance** than the iPhone 17 Pro.

The other major changes are battery life of up to **36 hours on the Pro and 45 hours on the Pro Max**, faster wired charging, the new Apple-designed **C2 cellular modem**, and a redesigned Dynamic Island capable of showing **three Live Activities simultaneously**.

## iPhone 18 Pro/Max vs iPhone 17 Pro/Max: Top 10 changes at a glance

The five biggest changes are the variable-aperture camera, A20 Pro, improved cooling, longer battery life and redesigned Dynamic Island/connectivity system. Here is an overview of what’s new compared to the previous generation.

| Feature | iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | iPhone 17 Pro / Pro Max | What’s changed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Main camera | 48MP, **variable ƒ/1.48–ƒ/4 aperture** | 48MP, fixed aperture | Major new photographic control |
| Processor | **A20 Pro, 2nm** | A19 Pro | New manufacturing process |
| GPU | 7-core, up to **40% faster** | 6-core | Significant graphics boost |
| Neural Engine | **Dual 16-core / 32 cores total** | 16-core | Around 2x AI compute |
| Cooling | Vapor chamber with **3x surface area** | First-gen vapor chamber | Up to 40% better sustained performance |
| Pro Max battery | **45 hours video** | 39 hours | +6 hours |
| Pro battery | **Up to 36 hours video** on eSIM model | 33 hours | Up to +3 hours |
| Wired charging | 50% in around **15 minutes** | 50% in around 20 minutes | Faster charging |
| Modem | **Apple C2** | Qualcomm modem | Apple-designed modem, lower power use |
| Dynamic Island | Redesigned, **3 Live Activities** | Previous design, up to 2 | More information displayed simultaneously |

Apple has added a 2TB option to the smaller Pro for the first time, while retaining 256GB as the entry-level capacity.

## iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Max release date: When will the new iPhones go on sale?

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max were announced on **Wednesday, September 9, 2026**.

Pre-orders start at **5 a.m. Pacific on Saturday, September 12**. That’s **1pm in the U.K.**

Both models will then go on sale on **Friday, September 18, 2026** in more than 65 countries and regions. Another 20 countries will get the phones from September 25.

You will be able to buy the phones directly from Apple online or at Apple Stores, as well as through mobile networks and authorized Apple retailers. Apple sells unlocked iPhones directly through its website and stores.

## iPhone 18 Pro/Max design: What does it look like?

![iPhone 18 Pro Burgundy](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/iPhone-18-Pro-Burgundy.jpeg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

This is the Burgundy variant (we think Deep Cherry was a much nicer name).

Apple

The iPhone 18 Pro retains the aluminium unibody introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro, as well as the Ceramic Shield on the rear and Ceramic Shield 2 over the display. The camera system remains arranged on the large raised plateau across the upper part of the rear casing.

Screen sizes are unchanged at **6.3 inches for the iPhone 18 Pro** and **6.9 inches for the iPhone 18 Pro Max**, both using Super Retina XDR OLED displays with ProMotion up to 120Hz.

Apple offers four finishes this year:

* **Burgundy**
* **Glacier**
* **Silver**
* **Black**

That means Cosmic Orange and Deep Blue disappear, while black returns to the Pro line despite pre-launch reports suggesting it would not.

The pre-event leaks suggested the basic chassis dimensions would remain very close to the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, with the camera plateau rather than the body itself becoming thicker.

The new iPhones share the same screen sizes and overall form as their predecessors, but both models are slightly heavier this time.

* **iPhone 18 Pro dimensions**: 150 x 71.9 x 8.75mm / 5.91 x 2.83 x 0.34 in
* **iPhone 18 Pro weight**: 7.44 ounces / 211 grams (17 Pro was 7.27 ounces / 206 grams)
* **iPhone 18 Pro** **Max dimensions**: 163.4 x 78 x 8.75mm / 6.43 x 3.07 x 0.34 in
* **iPhone 18 Pro Max weight**: 8.78 ounces / 249 grams (17 Pro Max was 8.22 ounces / 233 grams)

### Changes to the Dynamic Island

Apple has redesigned the Dynamic Island. Apple says new display technology creates additional usable space and allows the Dynamic Island to display **up to three Live Activities at once**, for example navigation, music and a sports score.

Apple has **not announced fully under-display Face ID**. Pre-launch reports suggested that one or more infrared Face ID components could move beneath the OLED panel, allowing the notch to shrink, but Apple hasn’t confirmed the underlying sensor arrangement.

## iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max cameras: Are the cameras the same?

![iPhone 18 Pro Cameras](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/iPhone-18-Pro-Cameras.jpeg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

The iPhone 18 Pro cameras.

Apple

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have the **same three-camera rear system**. The main change is not resolution—all three remain 48MP—but the new variable-aperture Main camera and new computational imaging pipeline.

The three most notable camera upgrades are:

1. **Variable aperture** on the 48MP Main camera.
2. A **new Main camera sensor and imaging pipeline**, improving low-light performance and detail.
3. More extensive **manual Pro controls**, including aperture, shutter speed, white balance and histogram.

### Rear cameras

| Camera | Resolution | Focal length | Aperture | Pixel information |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fusion Main | 48MP | 24mm / 48mm, 1x / 2x | **ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, ƒ/4 variable** | 2.44μm quad-pixel / 1.22μm individual |
| Fusion Ultra Wide | 48MP | 13mm, 0.5x / macro | ƒ/2.2 | 1.4μm quad-pixel / 0.7μm individual |
| Fusion Telephoto | 48MP | 100mm / 200mm, 4x / 8x | ƒ/2.8 | 1.4μm quad-pixel / 0.7μm individual |

The Main camera’s six-blade mechanical aperture can automatically open to **ƒ/1.48** in low light or close as far as **ƒ/4** for increased depth of field. Apple says the widest setting improves low-light performance by around 50%. Photographers can also select aperture manually.

Both Pro models also offer up to **8x optical-quality zoom** from the Telephoto camera. Contrary to some earlier rumors, the variable-aperture camera is **not exclusive to the Pro Max**.

### Front camera

Apple has retained the **18MP Center Stage front camera**, rather than moving to the rumored 24MP sensor. It supports automatic reframing, Center Stage, ultra-stabilized video and Dual Capture.

The front camera remains visibly associated with the Dynamic Island. Apple has not announced an under-display selfie camera on the iPhone 18 Pro.

### iPhone 18 Pro video changes

**Frame rates:** Cinematic effects can now be applied **after shooting** to ordinary videos captured at up to 60fps. The phones continue to offer **4K 120fps Dolby Vision** for high-frame-rate shooting.

**Time-lapse:** Time-lapse receives a significant upgrade to **4K with Dolby Vision HDR**.

**Computational photography:** Apple has introduced a new imaging pipeline, smart focus tracking, improved Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, an Extend tool and **Photographic Styles 3**, which adds texture and grain adjustments.

## A20 Pro processor: How fast is it?

![A20 Pro Processor](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/A20-Pro-Processor.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple has redesigned the iPhone chip.

Apple

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max use Apple’s new **A20 Pro** processor.

It is manufactured using a **2-nanometer process**, down from the 3nm-class process used for A19 Pro, giving Apple more scope to improve efficiency and transistor density.

The chip includes:

* **6-core CPU**
* **7-core GPU**
* Neural Accelerators integrated into the CPU/GPU architecture
* **Dual 16-core Neural Engine**, 32 cores in total
* **50% more memory bandwidth** than A19 Pro

Apple says the GPU is up to **40% faster than A19 Pro**, while the Neural Engine offers roughly **double the AI processing capability**.

One particularly important change is the packaging. Inspired by Apple’s M-series Mac chips, A20 Pro places the processor die **side-by-side with memory** rather than stacking memory directly in the chip’s thermal path. This improves heat transfer and allows the processor to couple more directly to the vapor chamber.

That vapor chamber itself has **three times the surface area** of the iPhone 17 Pro’s system. Apple claims the combination delivers up to **40% better sustained performance**, which should be most noticeable during gaming, video work and intensive on-device AI rather than ordinary web browsing and messaging.

## RAM: How much memory does the iPhone 18 Pro/Max have?

Apple does not officially publish RAM capacities for iPhones, and its launch material does not specify a RAM figure.

Reports ahead of the event indicated **12GB of RAM**, but importantly the iPhone 17 Pro was also widely reported to have 12GB. That means there may not be a capacity increase this generation.

The more important confirmed improvement is **50% higher memory bandwidth**, which allows the A20 Pro, GPU and Neural Engine to access data faster.

That is particularly relevant to Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Larger on-device AI models demand not only sufficient RAM but very high memory bandwidth, so Apple’s chip and packaging changes should allow more complex models to run locally and for longer without the same thermal constraints.

## iPhone 18 Pro/Max connectivity options

### C2 modem

One of the biggest changes is Apple’s **C2 cellular modem**, replacing the Qualcomm modem used in the previous Pro generation.

Apple says C2 delivers:

* Faster upload performance than C1X
* **15% lower energy consumption**
* AI-powered improvements to connection quality and reliability
* **mmWave support in the U.S.**

This confirms a major rumor from before the launch.

### Wi-Fi and Bluetooth

Like the predecessors, the 2026 iPhones use Apple’s **N1 wireless networking chip**, supporting:

* **Wi-Fi 7**
* **Bluetooth 6**
* **Thread**

### Satellite

Emergency SOS via satellite, Messages via satellite, Roadside Assistance via satellite and Find My satellite functionality continue. Apple made no announcements about full satellite internet or ordinary 5G data delivered by satellite, despite pre-launch rumors suggesting such a capability could appear.

## iPhone 18 Pro/Max Battery, MagSafe and charging: What’s changed?

Battery life is one of the most significant improvements.

Apple says eSIM-only models gain additional battery capacity because the space previously occupied by the physical SIM tray can be used for battery cells. Physical-SIM variants provide around **two hours less video playback** than equivalent eSIM-only models.

The improvement comes from a combination of larger batteries, the more efficient 2nm A20 Pro processor and lower-power C2 modem.

Apple rates **eSIM-only models** for up to:

| Model | iPhone 18 | iPhone 17 | Improvement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pro | **36 hours video playback** | 33 hours | Up to +3 hours |
| Pro Max | **45 hours video playback** | 39 hours | **+6 hours** |

### Wired charging

Wired charging is faster. The iPhone 18 Pro can reach **50% in around 15 minutes**, compared with around 20 minutes for the iPhone 17 Pro. Five minutes of wired charging can provide around seven hours of video playback on the Pro Max.

### MagSafe and wireless charging

Wireless charging can reach **50% in around 30 minutes**, which is broadly unchanged from the iPhone 17 Pro generation. There is therefore a wired-charging speed improvement, but Apple hasn’t announced a comparable jump in MagSafe charging speed.

## iPhone 18 Pro price: How much does it cost?

Apple has increased prices by **$100** in the U.S. and £100 in the U.K.

The iPhone 18 Pro starts at **$1,199/£1,199**, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at **$1,299/£1,299**. Both begin with 256GB of storage.

| Model | iPhone 18 starting price | iPhone 17 starting price | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone Pro | **$1,199/£1,199** | $1,099/£1,099 | +$100/£100 |
| iPhone Pro Max | **$1,299/£1,299** | $1,199/£1,199 | +$100/£100 |

Apple offers both models with **256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB**. That means the entry-level storage remains 256GB rather than increasing again. The notable change is that **2TB is now available on both models**; previously the iPhone 17 Pro topped out at 1TB while the Pro Max could be configured with 2TB.

The $100 increase is considerably smaller than some analyst predictions before launch. Those forecasts had pointed to sharply higher DRAM and NAND costs caused by the global memory shortage, with estimates that the cost of 12GB of DRAM alone could rise dramatically this year. That makes component and memory pricing a credible contributor to Apple’s increase, although Apple itself hasn’t attributed the higher price to any one component.

## Should you buy the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max? Which model should you choose?

![2026 iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2026-iPhone-18-Pro-and-Pro-Max.jpeg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Which one do you want?

Apple

The iPhone 18 Pro is a much stronger upgrade than the specifications initially suggest. The variable-aperture camera, A20 Pro, improved cooling, faster charging and better battery life all make meaningful differences, particularly for photography, gaming and intensive AI use. iPhone 17 Pro owners don’t need to rush to upgrade unless those features matter, but anyone coming from an iPhone 15 Pro or older will see a substantial jump. The **6.3-inch Pro is the better choice for most buyers** because it has the same cameras and processor. Choose the **Pro Max** mainly if you want its larger display and class-leading 45-hour video battery life.

entries.title: Apple just raised the price of every iPhone it sells
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

Apple announced its new high-end iPhones at its Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday. If you’ve been paying close attention, then one major announcement wasn’t a surprise: the price increases. The new iPhones that Apple introduced are more expensive than the models they replaced. And even the old ones all cost more too.

Back in June, [Apple raised prices for Macs and iPads](https://www.macworld.com/article/3176418/ugh-apples-price-hikes-are-brutal.html), but did not change iPhone prices. The thought was that the company would wait until the new iPhone release to raise prices. And that, they did–the increases for the new Pro models range from $1,199 for the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro to $2,499 for the 2TB iPhone 18 Pro Max. Here’s a look at the new pricing and how they differ from the models they replace.

| Model | New Price | Previous Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone Ultra (256GB) | $1,999 | — |
| iPhone 18 Pro (256GB) | $1,199 | $1,099 |
| iPhone 18 Pro (512GB) | $1,399 | $1,299 |
| iPhone 18 Pro (1TB) | $1,799 | $1,499 |
| iPhone 18 Pro (2TB) | $2,399 | — |
| iPhone 18 Pro Max (256GB) | $1,299 | $1,199 |
| iPhone 18 Pro Max (512GB) | $1,499 | $1,399 |
| iPhone 18 Pro Max (1TB) | $1,899 | $1,599 |
| iPhone 18 Pro Max (2TB) | $2,499 | $1,999 |
| iPhone 17 (256GB) | $899 | $799 |
| iPhone 17 (512GB) | $1,099 | $999 |
| iPhone 17e (256GB) | $699 | $599 |
| iPhone 17e (512GB) | $899 | $799 |
| iPhone Air (256GB) | $1,099 | $999 |
| iPhone Air (512GB) | $1,299 | $1,199 |
| iPhone Air (1TB) | $1,699 | $1,399 |
| iPhone 16 (128GB) | $799 | $699 |
| iPhone 16 Plus (128GB) | N/A | $799 |
| iPhone 16 Plus (256GB) | N/A | $899 |

Basically, every iPhone now costs $100 more at the starting price and significantly more than that when you get into higher storage tiers. For example, Apple is charging iPhone 18 Pro Max buyers a whopping $599 more to jump to 2TB of storage. Even the iPhone 16 costs more and the Plus, which previously started at $799, is gone from the lineup.

The price hikes even affect the models that weren’t updated today. The iPhone 17 now starts at $899 and the iPhone 17e jumped to $699. Those are pretty big price jumps that should mean the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e coming next spring shouldn’t get another hike. But in this world of memory crunching, who knows?

entries.title: US Agencies Warn Chinese AI Firms Are Extracting Advanced AI Models
entries.content:
## **US agencies accuse six Chinese AI firms of extracting billions of tokens from US AI models to accelerate development and copy advanced capabilities.**

NSA, CISA, and the FBI jointly published [an advisory](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa26-251a) accusing six Chinese AI companies, [DeepSeek](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/deepseek), Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and [Z.AI](https://Z.AI), of running industrial-scale extraction campaigns against US frontier models since at least late 2024. The framing is deliberate: this isn’t a footnote to how these companies build AI, the agencies call it the core of their entire development strategy.

Distillation is a legitimate and widely used technique. It involves training a smaller AI model to reproduce the answers and capabilities of a larger one. But the advisory says the activity it uncovered went much further. It alleges that the companies sent millions of requests to models such as Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok and extracted billions of tokens.

*“China-based artificial intelligence (AI) companies are conducting systematic extraction of proprietary functionalities and capabilities of U.S. AI companies’ models through industrial-scale knowledge distillation campaigns that form the core—not merely a supplement—of their AI development strategy.” [states the report](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa26-251a). “Likely with Chinese government awareness, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and Z.AI extracted billions of tokens across millions of exchanges/requests from U.S. frontier AI models, including variants of Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok, since at least late 2024.”*

The goal was to capture valuable capabilities, including reasoning, coding, and agentic skills that took years and huge amounts of computing power to develop.

The advisory provides the most detail about DeepSeek. It claims the company ran an organized campaign against different versions of Claude, GPT, and Gemini between late 2024 and mid-2025 to help develop its R1 and V3 models. The extracted data reportedly included specialized knowledge, such as legal expertise, as well as chain-of-thought reasoning.

*“Advanced industrial-scale distillation tactics include chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning extraction, automated failover between pathways during blocking attempts, and sophisticated quality evaluation frameworks to detect defensive countermeasures. China-based AI companies that conduct industrial-scale distillation against U.S.” continues the advisory. “AI models see significantly shorter AI development timelines and reduced financial expenditures in training a frontier model.”*

This is particularly significant because AI companies usually limit access to a model’s internal reasoning. Getting a model to reveal those steps could therefore give attackers much more than just its final answers.

Moonshot AI’s alleged operation shows how fast these campaigns can move once new models ship. The advisory states the company redirected its extraction traffic to a newly released Claude model within 24 hours of launch, which only works if you already have infrastructure sitting ready and monitoring provider releases in real time. That’s not opportunistic scraping; that’s a standing operation built specifically to capture whatever comes out next.

The methods described in the advisory suggest a highly organized operation rather than researchers simply making API requests. The companies allegedly bought large numbers of premium accounts and shared them among teams of developers running many sessions at the same time. They also routed traffic through gray-market proxy services, which the advisory calls “transfer stations,” to remove identifying information and avoid detection. StepFun reportedly used pools of accounts and automated systems to spread requests across them, helping bypass rate limits and increase daily spending as the operation grew.

The advisory also describes attempts to manipulate the AI models themselves. MiniMax allegedly used prompt injection to convince Claude Code that it was actually a MiniMax product, hoping to make it behave differently. While this detail may sound unusual, it shows how far some of these efforts reportedly went to extract information from competing AI systems.

The advisory doesn’t just name and shame, it lays out concrete detection signals for US AI companies to watch for. Shared accounts logging in from multiple IPs and user agents, usage running 24/7 without the natural idle periods a human would produce, subscription-to-API-usage ratios that don’t add up, and brand-new accounts hitting maximum usage immediately instead of ramping up gradually the way legitimate adoption normally does.

We must consider that any one of those signals alone might be nothing, but the agencies are betting the combination is a fairly reliable tell.

*“China-based AI companies leverage techniques not in MITRE ATLAS, demonstrating significant organizational investment, operational maturity, and adaptive capability development distinguishing these campaigns from opportunistic exploitation.” added the advisory.*

The recommended countermeasures get genuinely aggressive, and one in particular is worth sitting with. The advisory suggests quietly serving degraded, less capable responses to accounts suspected of running distillation campaigns, without ever telling those users their access has been downgraded, specifically so they can’t adjust their extraction technique in response. That’s a notable policy stance from a government advisory: not just detect and block, but actively deceive suspected bad actors about the quality of what they’re receiving.

Whatever the geopolitical debate, the practical lesson for companies using frontier AI models is clear. If several employees share enterprise AI accounts, providers will likely monitor usage more closely for the patterns described in the advisory. Heavy legitimate use could sometimes trigger false positives, especially when organizations have many developers making large numbers of requests at the same time.

**Follow me on Twitter:**[**@securityaffairs**](https://twitter.com/securityaffairs)**and**[**Facebook**](https://www.facebook.com/sec.affairs)**and**[**Mastodon**](https://infosec.exchange/@securityaffairs)

[**Pierluigi Paganini**](http://www.linkedin.com/pub/pierluigi-paganini/b/742/559)

**(**[**SecurityAffairs**](http://securityaffairs.co/wordpress/)**– hacking, AI Models)**

entries.title: Apple Launches iPhone 18 Pro With Variable-Aperture Camera System
entries.content:
Apple's iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max were announced today and keep last year's overall design but put the emphasis on camera upgrades, including a 48-megapixel variable-aperture system, new manual controls, and 4K Dolby Vision recording. Prices for the devices start at $1,199 and $1,299, respectively. TechCrunch reports: The new Pro series camera features a 48-megapixel camera with variable aperture, made with six thin blades. This system will likely improve low-light photography quality and speed. There are also new pro controls in the camera software, including white balance, shutter speed, aperture and histogram. There are also new photographic styles with texture and grain controls. [...]
The new camera can record 4K videos in Dolby HDR Vision, and also apply cinematic effects after shooting the footage. The new Pro devices also have a smaller dynamic range island on the front of the device, which now allows you to track three live activities instead of two.
Both phones are powered by Apple's latest A20 Pro silicon and feature a newly designed vapor chamber for improved cooling. The company has also improved the battery with a better design. Apple also said the iPhone 18 Pro supports video playback of 36 hours, and the 18 Pro Max has 45 hours of playback capacity. Apple Unveils the iPhone Duo, Its First Foldable iPhone

entries.title: Women came together in London to talk about building careers in AI, how they got here, what comes ne...
entries.content:
Women came together in London to talk about building careers in AI, how they got here, what comes next, and what it takes to move forward in a field that’s changing fast.  
  
Replit and our partners at the Incubator for Artificial Intelligence, the UK Government’s Incubator for Artificial Intelligence, brought together women already working in AI and women looking to find their way into the field.  
  
The more people who bring different skills, experiences, and perspectives to the field, the better we can shape what comes next.  
  
That’s what Replit and the Incubator for Artificial Intelligence are working toward in different ways: building AI that expands what people can do, from making software development more accessible to improving public services.  
  
The future of AI should be built by more people, and women should be at the center of that future.

entries.title:
苹果刚刚发布了它的首款折叠手机，iPhone Duo  ​​​​https://t.co/afzxygqaQ8

Apple 今天在 Apple Park 举办"Surprise and Shine"...
entries.content:
苹果刚刚发布了它的首款折叠手机，iPhone Duo ​​​​[x.com/TheAppleDesign…](https://x.com/TheAppleDesign/status/2097751929925624173/video/1)  
  
Apple 今天在 Apple Park 举办"Surprise and Shine"发布会，这是新任 CEO John Ternus 上任以来的第一场重大产品发布。Ternus 于 9 月 1 日正式接替 Tim Cook，后者转任执行董事长。Cook 本人也坐在了发布会前排。  
  
发布会的核心是两款手机：Apple 第一款折叠屏 iPhone Duo，以及 iPhone 18 Pro 系列。  
  
iPhone Duo：Apple 的第一款折叠屏  
  
传了好几年的折叠 iPhone 终于来了。iPhone Duo 采用书本式折叠设计，展开后形似护照，内屏 7.6 英寸，外屏 5.4 英寸。机身用的是 5 级钛金属，IP68 防尘防水。  
  
芯片和 iPhone 18 Pro 一样是 A20 Pro，搭配 Apple 自研的 C2 基带。后置双 48MP 摄像头，没有长焦镜头，这是相比 18 Pro 最明显的妥协，大概率是为了控制机身厚度。生物识别用的是侧边按钮的 Touch ID，而非 Face ID，也可以用 Apple Watch 解锁。后续还会支持 Apple Pencil。  
  
两个颜色：星光白和夜空色。256GB 起售价 2,000 美元，最高配置大约 3,000 美元。今天只是发布，预计最早 10 月开售，比 iPhone 18 Pro 晚一步。  
  
对比三星 Galaxy Z Fold 系列（同样 256GB 起售价 1,999 美元），Apple 在价格上基本持平，但在折叠屏市场已经是后来者，三星和华为在这个品类经营了七年。  
  
iPhone 18 Pro：2nm 芯片和可变光圈  
  
iPhone 18 Pro 和 Pro Max 搭载 A20 Pro 芯片，2nm 工艺，2 个"桌面级"超级核心加 4 个能效核心，7 核 GPU。散热性能提升到上一代的三倍。  
  
摄像头最大的变化是 48MP 主摄支持可变光圈，简单说就是镜头可以自动调节进光量和景深，拍人像和夜景时效果会明显提升。还有一个新功能：手机可以验证一张照片没有被 AI 编辑过，在 AI 生成内容满天飞的时代，这算是一个实用的信任工具。  
  
Dynamic Island 缩小了，同时最多支持三个实时活动同步显示。Pro Max 续航提升到 30 小时，充电 15 分钟可以到 50%，这是 iPhone 有史以来最大的电池提升幅度。  
  
四个新颜色：黑色、浅蓝、冰川色（银）、勃艮第（红）。Pro 起售价 1,199 美元，Pro Max 起售价 1,299 美元，均为 256GB 起步。9 月 12 日开始预购，9 月 18 日发售。  
  
其他产品  
  
AirPods 5 的降噪比 AirPods 4 提升了 50%。两个版本：基础版 129 美元带主动降噪，高配版 149 美元多了耳柄音量控制、更长续航和无线充电盒。今天开始预购。  
  
Apple Watch Series 12（399 美元起）和 Ultra 4（799 美元起）升级了健康追踪系统，Series 12 重新引入了陶瓷材质。新增了一个叫 Siri Recap 的功能，用环境监听为你整理一天的高级别笔记。今天预购。  
  
iOS 27 的正式推送日期确认为 9 月 14 日。  
  
值得注意的是，今年普通版的 iPhone 18、iPhone Air 2 和 iPhone 18e 被推到了 2027 年春季，Apple 把九月发布会的焦点完全集中在了高端产品线上。

"The lab...
entries.content:
Vals AI CEO Rayan Krishnan on why defensible evals are critical for enterprises' survival:  
  
"The labs side of it is very clear. If you're raising lots of money, investing heavily in building models, it's essential for you to show why your model is getting better and why the customer should pay a premium for them."  
  
"But what I think is still underappreciated is, on the enterprise side, this is turning out to be existential as well."  
  
"We're in this world where it is still very unclear what ROI looks like and how to value this intelligence that's being used... Token spend may start to eclipse salary spend."  
  
"If this is such a meaningful line item in your costs, you have to justify the ROI much more cleanly... Over time, I think a firm really is just its evals."  
  
"The ability for a company to make its evals legible in order to solve this ROI calculus is going to be the reason why that company wins out over its competitors in the long term."  
  
[@RayanKrishnan](https://x.com/RayanKrishnan)[@eriktorenberg](https://x.com/eriktorenberg)

[Your browser does not support the video tag.](https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2097753152904896512/vid/avc1/1920x1080/6fUujvunFU2tYQ9p.mp4?tag=16)

[🔗 View on Twitter](https://x.com/a16z/status/2097753236715499816/video/1)

![a16z](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/1919488160125616128/QAZXTMEj_normal.png)

a16z@a16z

Vals AI co-founder and CEO Rayan Krishnan with a16z's Ben Horowitz and Jennifer Li on grading AI, what it costs, and who gets to make the rules:  
  
Every big industry eventually grows an independent testing layer. AI has credit ratings to learn from and Enron to avoid. Model capability today is still mostly self-reported.  
  
As public benchmarks saturate and models get better at optimizing for the tests themselves, Rayan makes the case for independent, continuously evolving evaluations.  
  
The harder problem is geopolitical. Reagan's "trust but verify" worked during the Cold War because you could fly over and count the missiles. No simple equivalent for AI models exists.  
  
In this conversation with Erik Torenberg, they get into how you measure a model's ability to improve itself, why every good benchmark eventually has to be retired, and what happens when token spend begins to rival employee salaries.

A tiny TypeScript web agent, built with Astra and improved through real browser evals.  
  
We’ve built Browser Use, Browser Harness and BrowserCode. This time we asked Astra to combine what worked, with as little code and as few heuristics as possible. Then Astra hill climbed:  
  
> Run real browser tasks  
> Read traces  
> Fix what breaks  
> Delete complexity  
> Run again and repeat.

entries.title:
Better models don’t automatically mean smaller AI bills.

Sometimes they mean you finally have a rea...
entries.content:
Better models don’t automatically mean smaller AI bills.  
  
Sometimes they mean you finally have a reason to run the workflow you couldn’t get working before.   
  
That’s what makes GPT-6 Astra interesting to me.   
  
Once a model can research, build, inspect, and refine, you start giving it more ambitious tasks. A single response becomes an entire working session.   
  
The useful question is no longer just “what does a million tokens cost?”   
  
It’s “what can I get done with this budget?”   
  
That’s also why cashback on inference is worth paying attention to. On work you were already going to run, getting some of the spend back gives you a choice: keep the savings or fund another experiment.   
  
But the goal should never be to burn more tokens.   
  
It should be to get more verified, useful work out of the same budget.

Yesterday, Anthropic's alignment science lead put a >10% chance on AI killing all humans within a decade.  
  
For some lighter reading, Anthropic's economics team just published what happens to the U.S. economy if it doesn't.  
  
Three scenarios for 2030, GDP measured against a world without AI:  
  
- Modest: AI's impact is "something like the internet's." GDP +1.6%.  
  
- Substantial: AI can do half of all knowledge work, most of it on its own. GDP +8.3%. Knowledge-worker wages "essentially flat."  
  
- Extreme: AI does nearly all knowledge work. GDP +32.4% (!) to $44.4T, growth hits 15% a year, and the economy doubles every 4.5 years.

entries.title: 苹果 iOS / iPadOS 27、macOS 27、watchOS 27 和 visionOS 27 定档 9 月 15 日推出
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，苹果官网显示，iOS / iPadOS 27、macOS 27、watchOS 27 和 visionOS 27 **将于 9 月 15 日推出**。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/b6b28f36-d806-4389-a55b-94ef5bbf8b7f.jpg)

据介绍，苹果全新一代 OS 设计一再演进。Liquid Glass 折射效果更均匀，对比度更出色，确保内容清晰易读。还新加了调节滑块，用户可随心调整 Liquid Glass 的外观效果。同时，iPhone 和 iPad App 拥有更快的启动速度，隔空投送传输表现更迅捷。

Apple Watch 拥有更多小组件，会适时现身智能叠放来帮忙。方便用户及时发送生日祝福，查看停车位置，赶在节假日前改掉睡眠闹钟，或是置顶交通卡来快速查余额。Apple Vision Pro 支持通知消息一眼展开。只需眼睛看一看，就能快速预览通知。当这条通知弹出时，直接注视就能展开更多内容，还可进一步操作。

IT之家注意到，苹果还全新规划了少儿安全防护措施，进一步升级、拓展了各项功能，让家长和监护人能轻松守护孩子上网安全：通过“设置助理”，家长可以决定具体开放哪些系统 App 给孩子使用；全新的“请求浏览”功能支持孩子只有经过许可才能访问新网站；“通信安全”有助于防止孩子在信息和 FaceTime 通话等 App 中查看或分享裸露内容。

## 如何升级 iOS / iPadOS / watchOS / macOS 开发版和公测版？

• **公开测试版**：需注册 [Apple Beta 版软件计划](https://beta.apple.com/zh-CN/guide#ios "Apple Beta 版软件计划")，之后通过【设置】【通用】【软件更新】【Beta 版更新】来升级；

• **开发预览版**：需登录注册[苹果开发者计划](https://developer.apple.com/programs/ "苹果开发者计划")，之后通过【设置】【通用】【软件更新】来升级。

entries.title: 苹果 watchOS 27.0 RC 发布
entries.content:
【[点此直达升级教程](https://www.ithome.com/1/000/529.htm#profile-download)】

IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，苹果今日向 Apple Watch 用户推送了 watchOS 27.0 RC 更新（内部版本号：24R363），本次更新距离上次发布 Beta / RC 间隔 9 天，正式版将于 9 月 15 日发布。

苹果 watchOS 27 主要聚焦升级 Siri AI、健康追踪、健身辅导与智能叠放（Smart Stack）。在 Siri AI 方面，底层由 Apple Intelligence 驱动，支持开放式问题与更自然的多轮对话。用户可直接在手腕上询问跑后恢复拉伸建议，也可连续追问相关内容。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/6/71c96648-0417-4c78-b980-d10a1f49749d.jpg)

Siri AI 还能调用备忘录等个人内容，帮助查找驾照号码、租住房屋门禁码等已存信息，减少用户频繁拿起 iPhone 的需要。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/6/2cefdcd8-27a9-476a-88e8-97ec600981bf.jpg)

健康追踪方面，苹果 watchOS 27 扩展经期健康支持，符合条件的用户可收到与围绝经期相关的周期偏差提醒。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/6/b729da7d-9493-49a1-ac74-5ab0db02e3e0.jpg)

IT之家注：围绝经期指女性在绝经前后，身体逐步过渡到绝经状态的一段时期，月经周期和身体感受可能出现波动。

在跑步追踪方面，苹果补充了与配速、距离和锻炼时长相关的新数据，让用户能更清楚地观察长期表现变化。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/6/b7f0e2f8-85ff-4985-aae9-2739bcd517db.jpg)

在健身辅导方面，苹果 watchOS 27 同步升级 Workout Buddy（运动伙伴），新增西班牙语支持，并可依据用户过往健身历史给出更个性化的激励与反馈。此外用户在锻炼时使用 Workout Buddy 不再需要随身携带 iPhone。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/6/30961652-137b-493e-b096-72308c34e933.png)

界面层面，watchOS 27 也强化了单手操作与信息前置能力，新手势支持用户用拇指和食指轻点 1 次，快速选取小组件并查看信息。

智能叠放（Smart Stack）则获得更强的情境感知能力，可按活动状态和即时需求主动展示内容，比如亲近联系人的生日提醒、停车位置，以及假日前的睡眠闹钟调整建议。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/6/6753ca7c-68b7-4d54-bb7f-4e3c2398266f.jpg)

## 如何升级 iOS / iPadOS / watchOS / macOS 开发版和公测版？

• **公开测试版**：需注册 [Apple Beta 版软件计划](https://beta.apple.com/zh-CN/guide#ios "Apple Beta 版软件计划")，之后通过【设置】【通用】【软件更新】【Beta 版更新】来升级；

entries.title: Apple’s new iPhone camera mode promises to prove your photo isn’t AI
entries.content:
![A photo of the iPhone 18 Pro](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/268734_iPhone_2026_event_handson_ADiBenedetto_0023.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Apple is [launching a new way](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-debuts-iphone-18-pro-and-iphone-18-pro-max/) to prove that the picture you took isn't manipulated by AI. A new feature, called "Reference Image," will arrive with the iPhone 18 Pro lineup later this month and is supposed to use the device's new camera sensor to "sign every pixel it sees."

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will only authenticate photos when placed into Reference mode. Once the camera captures signed sensor data, Apple says its Private Cloud Compute will develop it "into an unalterable reference image" that can be viewed in the Photos app. You'll be able to compare the reference image with other versions of the photo to see if any edits were mad …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/tech/992766/apple-iphone-18-pro-reference-image)
