Android Studio Quail 4 稳定版现已正式发布！本次核心更新深度整合了 Android 官方团队精选的 AI Skills，并原生集成 Gemma 4 本地模型。无需繁琐配置即可享受，全面加速开发与重构工作流。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=02911a83&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2Fbyib5ZoSZw3H9pSqrevIk52NeiazV2nkQbB8bklqZNSkFIt5Tb3EXTT0jrKL0fNfsuqsibZJMKM51CszLG755UuV7bIJrljbAiaEzZkgTiajP0V0%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg%23imgIndex%3D0)

作者 / Android Studio 产品经理 Amman Fasil Asfaw

Android Studio Quail 4 现已推出稳定版，可供您在生产环境中使用。

这是 Android Studio Quail 的最终稳定版本。您可借助 Android Studio 中的新功能，高速且有效地使用 AI 构建高质量应用。您可观看以下视频，了解最近 4 个版本中的实用新功能如何帮助您进一步优化并加速开发流程。

以下是对 Android Studio Quail 4 新功能的深度介绍: 

**内置于 Android Studio 中的**

**Android Skills**

虽然 LLM 在通用编码查询方面展现出了惊人的能力，但在面对快速迭代的 Android API、平台专属的迁移或复杂的配置结构时，它们往往会生成错误或过时的代码。为解决这个问题，我们将 Android 开发团队整理出来的精选 Android Skills 内置到了 Android Studio 中。这些都是针对 AI 优化的模块化指令，遵循开放标准的 Agent Skills 规范，专用于指导 LLM 完成复杂的 Android 工作流。Android Skills 现已预置在 IDE 中，开箱即用，无需手动下载其他文件。

* Android Skills

  <https://developer.android.com/tools/agents/android-skills>
* Agent Skills 规范

  <https://agentskills.io/>

当您向 Android Studio 智能体发出提示词时，系统会分析您的提示内容，并根据已安装 Skills 的元数据进行搜索，然后在最相关的场景下自动调用相应 Skills。您的智能体可以即时获得领域专业知识、遵循 Google 的最佳实践，从而减少长时间手动设置提示词带来的花费。

Android Studio 已预加载 23 项精选 Skills: 

* 需要构建升级方面的帮助？可使用 Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) 9 Upgrade Skills。
* 想要分析应用的性能问题？可使用 Android Profiler Skills。
* 准备升级 Jetpack Navigation 框架？可使用 Navigation3 Skills。
* 想要让应用界面适配不同的 Android 设备？可使用 Adaptive Skills。

我们还建议您创建自己的自定义 Skills，为智能体模式扩展专业经验和定制化工作流。如果您想在 Android Studio 之外将 Android Skills 与其他的命令行界面 (CLI) AI 工具一起使用，请安装 Android CLI 并运行 android skills add --all 以快速上手。如果您想完全禁用内置 Skills，也可通过设置中的全局开关轻松关闭。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=9d813805&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2Fbyib5ZoSZw3Fg1zRick4rxAllRf99LhFUSklE7VVYhZ02hbmyibObxVp4oOXYzK16XjUkySicd6mTPhKDWiaDLGlvHyuibanYLGPILra9wXbBTxbA%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg%23imgIndex%3D12)

△ Android Studio 已预装 23 项精选 Android Skills

* 23 项精选 Skills

  <https://developer.android.com/tools/agents/android-skills/browse>
* Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) 9 Upgrade Skills

  <https://github.com/android/skills/tree/main/build-system/agp/agp-9-upgrade>
* Android Profiler 

  <https://github.com/android/skills/tree/main/profilers/android-profiler>
* Navigation3

  <https://github.com/android/skills/tree/main/navigation/navigation-3>
* Adaptive

  <https://github.com/android/skills/tree/main/jetpack-compose/adaptive>
* 创建自己的自定义 Skills

  <https://developer.android.com/studio/gemini/skills>

****Gemma 4 本地模型集成****

****(私密、安全的离线 AI 编码)****

许多开发者偏好使用本地模型，Android Studio 现已原生集成 Gemma 4 (Google 最强大的开放模型)，让您无需手动进行第三方设置即可获得 AI 代码辅助。

* 系统要求: 只需 12GB RAM 即可运行最小规格的模型，但建议配备 32GB 以上内存的设备以获得最佳运行体验。请参阅硬件要求。
* 一键式管理: 只需在 Agent 模型选择器中选择 Gemma，然后选择要下载的模型，或前往 Settings > Tools > AI > Model Providers > Gemma。Android Studio 会自动为您下载、验证和更新模型权重。
* 内置推理引擎: 我们内置了一个轻量级推理引擎，可直接在 IDE 中运行 Gemma 4 模型。
* 端侧 AI 智能体: 由于 Gemma 4 具备原生智能体工具调用能力，您可以使用完全离线的智能体运行复杂的多文件重构计划。您的源代码永远不会离开本地设备，也无需担心 Token 配额限制。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=b9b0c1c7&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2Fbyib5ZoSZw3HlCQWQdy5ymM1NGpQnMRibuk64KibOqXIkmranUy0rpdj8rbfVNKRTAavHRaTfz7Q3CQ1pY4aqmDmN86W0QLicnsReZVIr5Kwjrw%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg%23imgIndex%3D22)

△ 选择您要下载和使用的 Gemma 模型

* 硬件要求

  <https://developer.android.com/studio/gemini/use-a-local-model#try-the-gemma-4-model>

**并行智能体 UX 通知**

**和其他增强功能**

在 Android Studio Quail 2 中，我们推出了支持并行会话的智能体多任务处理功能。现在，Android Studio Quail 4 又带来了几项界面增强功能，旨在让您的 AI 交互更顺畅、更快捷、更透明: 

* 回复中的代码符号支持超链接: 系统现在会自动检测智能体回复中提到的类名、函数、方法和文件路径，并将其呈现为可点击的超链接。
* 实时后台智能体通知: 在并行处理多个会话任务时，"Recent Chats" 面板会提供让人一目了然的状态指示器。当智能体正在主动运行工具时，您将看到一个加载旋转图标；如果智能体正在等待您的输入，您将看到一个红色状态指示器；当后台任务完成且等待审查时，您将看到一个蓝色标记。
* 统一的变更摘要: 现在，当智能体完成多步骤编码任务后，单独的 Task 和 Walkthrough 已被整合到一个清晰、专用的 "Summary of Changes" 选项卡中，以便在应用修改之前为您提供清晰的差异对比和审核体验。
* 思考过程折叠渲染: 对于推理模型，智能体的逐步思考过程会被整齐的组织成可折叠的区块，使您的聊天对话易于浏览，同时又允许您按需检查底层逻辑。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=79876329&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2Fbyib5ZoSZw3E4YwjFdztNr5FV7hFsFQfFlNGNpsVTlO9qenBSVX5eb5r7ngXZWvsk8SHTPCwluvalmGnR6190Zibv83PKCIrJIB0btlAtCKgw%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg%23imgIndex%3D31)

△ 现在，您可以在 "Recent Chats" 面板中实时监控并行会话的进度

* 支持并行会话的智能体多任务处理功能

  <https://developer.android.com/blog/posts/android-studio-quail-2-is-stable-multi-task-with-the-android-studio-ai-agent>

**升级以获得高级 AI 能力**

Android Studio 为开发者提供了开箱即用的默认 Gemini 模型接入。我们会动态调整此模型的能力，以确保我们能够免费提供出色的体验。不过，如果您想要更精细地访问 Gemini 最强大的模型，或者需要额外的配额来进行长时间的编码会话，您可以使用以下 3 种途径之一升级您的访问权限: 

* API 密钥: 在获得可用的 Google AI Studio API 密钥后，您便可以在开发流程中使用最新的 Gemini 模型，例如 Gemini 3.7 Flash。您也可以在 Android Studio 中直接使用其他模型提供商 (如 Anthropic 或 OpenAI) 的 API 密钥。
* Google AI plan: 使用 Google AI Pro 或 Ultra plan 的开发者可以使用其 Google 帐户登录，以自动解锁高级配额和更高的速率限制。凭借其扩展能力，Gemini 可助您在大型代码库中分析、重构和规划功能。
* Gemini Enterprise: 如果您的组织有权访问 Gemini Enterprise，开发者可以在使用 Android Studio AI 智能体时登录，以利用 Google Cloud 的隐私和安全优势。此功能正面向特定组织推出，目前已在最新的 Android Studio Canary 中提供。

* Google AI Studio API 密钥

  <https://developer.android.com/studio/gemini/add-api-key>
* 其他模型提供商 (如 Anthropic 或 OpenAI) 的 API 密钥

  <https://developer.android.com/studio/gemini/use-a-remote-model>
* Google AI Pro 或 Ultra plan

  <https://one.google.com/ai?g1_landing_page=75&utm_source=android_studio&utm_campaign=android_studio_settings&pli=1>
* Gemini Enterprise

  <https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise>
* Canary

  <http://d.android.com/studio/preview/features#gemini-enterprise>

**Android Studio Quail 系列**

**总结回顾**

Android Studio Quail 4 体现了我们对于借助 AI 加速开发者生产力的持续努力。您可以查看我们之前的博文，进一步了解最近推出的新功能。

****Android Studio Quail****

* App Quality Insights 智能体集成: 在 Android Studio Quail 版本的开发周期伊始，我们就实现了 App Quality Insights (AQI) 与 Gemini 的深度集成。
* 在 Google I/O 大会上发布的 Android Studio Quail (Canary) 中: 我们推出了专为智能体时代打造的工具，包括 Agent Skills、Firebase 集成和智能体模式下的并行对话、Gemma 4 的本地模型支持、Android CLI、点对点 Android 模拟器多设备测试、ADB Wi-Fi 2.0 以及原生支持将应用发布至 Google Play 的测试轨道。

* Android Studio Quail

  <https://android-developers.googleblog.com/2026/05/whats-new-android-developer-tools.html>

****Android Studio Quail 2****

* 并行会话: 我们在 IDE 中解锁了并发多任务处理能力。开发者能够以并排编辑器标签页的形式开启多个会话 —— 例如，使用 Gemini 3.5 Flash 在一个标签页中运行 Compose 重构，同时在第二个标签页中使用 Gemma 4 生成代码文档。通过 "Recent Chats" 侧边栏中的实时进度指示器 (加载旋转图标、暂停状态和错误提示)，可轻松监控活动的后台任务。
* LeakCanary 性能分析: 我们直接将 LeakCanary 原生集成到了 Android Studio Profiler 中。通过将 JVM 堆分析工作从测试设备端剥离，转而在主机上运行 Shark 分析器引擎，内存泄漏追踪速度提高了五倍且完全无卡顿，还得到了 "Fix with Agent" AI 修复措施的支持。

* Android Studio Quail 2

  <https://developer.android.com/blog/posts/android-studio-quail-2-is-stable-multi-task-with-the-android-studio-ai-agent>

****Android Studio Quail 3****

* 简化 Planning 模式: 使用 /plan 命令或将会话切换到 "Planning" 时，智能体会回退一步以评估其逻辑，在编写代码之前制定实施计划。
* MCP Marketplace: 您现在可通过导航到 Settings > Tools > AI > MCP Servers，直接在 IDE 内轻松搜索、安装和管理模型上下文协议 (MCP) 服务器，您可借此将 AI 智能体连接到外部开发者工具、注册表和自定义数据库。

* Android Studio Quail 3

  <https://developer.android.com/studio/releases/past-releases/as-quail-3-release-notes>

**即刻体验**

Android Studio Quail 4 现已在稳定版渠道正式发布。告别手动配置，在并行线程中处理多任务，并使用专家级 AI 智能进行构建。

entries.title: Powering AI is an architecture problem
entries.content:
On July 22, 2026, a transmission line fault in Ashburn, Virginia—the heart of the world’s largest data center cluster—knocked [more than 3 gigawatts of load](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/outages/fault-in-data-center-alley-triggered-3-gw-load-drop-on-pjm) off the grid in seconds. And it wasn’t the first time. Two years earlier, a single failed surge arrester dropped [roughly 60 Virginia facilities and 1,500 megawatts](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/virginia-narrowly-avoided-power-cuts-when-60-data-centers-dropped-off-the-grid-at-once/) at once. No one could anticipate so much uniform load responding to grid faults the same way, at the same time.

![](https://wp.technologyreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ON-contributed-image.jpg?w=840)

The AI power debate is mostly about generation: more turbines, more solar, more transmission. The grid needs more electrons. But the outages in Virginia weren’t supply failures; they were architecture failures. And a giant wave of interconnections is arriving on that same architecture, putting grid reliability at risk. It’s a problem nobody wants to own.

### **Asking more from the grid**

The grid was built around predictable loads: steel mills, refineries, and houses at dinnertime. Different load sizes, same process—drawing power smoothly, misbehaving occasionally, and recovering gracefully.

But AI data centers don’t behave that way.

An AI campus can swing 70% of its load in milliseconds during a training run, then trip offline just as fast at the first sign of trouble upstream to protect billions in compute. Each is rational alone. Together, at gigawatt scale, they’re a problem the grid has never solved—and the next wave of data center campuses is planned at exactly that scale.

### **Where the old stack breaks**

The standard data center power stack hasn’t changed in decades. Medium-voltage power arrives, transformers step it down, low-voltage uninterruptible power supply (UPS) units condition it, and it reaches the racks. Push that design to AI scale, and it cracks in three places.

First, the UPS sits deep inside the building, close to the racks. But its batteries are an undersized spare tire, designed to handle an outage for a few minutes, not to absorb load swings this fast and volatile around the clock.

Second, the UPS spends most of its life in bypass. Legacy converters waste enough power that operators run in eco-mode: A static switch feeds the racks directly from the grid and nothing filters in either direction. The compute’s swings go out raw, and grid transients—sub-millisecond events that can damage or take down equipment—come in too fast for any switch to catch.

Third, the protection logic was written when “large load” meant 50 megawatts. This protection logic can’t see the grid it is now a part of, so when trouble hits upstream, it does exactly the wrong thing: it drops out. [In the 2024 Virginia event, most of the lost load traced to protection schemes that count voltage dips and disconnect on the third one](https://www.modernpowersystems.com/analysis/nerc-review-of-major-load-loss-and-data-centre-impact/)—as designed, at the worst moment.

This isn’t sloppy engineering. It’s careful engineering the load has outgrown.

### **Moving into the path**

The fix is three moves, made together.

**Move it up**—from 480 volts to medium voltage (13.8 kilovolts and higher), the voltage large sites draw from the grid.

**Move it out**—from the data hall to modular enclosures near the substation so the building holds only compute and the cooling that keeps it alive.

**Move it into the path**—instead of a battery that watches and reacts, a system every electron runs through, all the time. There’s nothing to detect and nothing to switch because nothing was ever routed around it.

On paper, three straightforward upgrades. In practice, they rewrite every line item downstream.

### **Making the change**

When thousands of GPUs spin up together, the system absorbs the swing and hands the grid a flat load profile. When a disturbance hits, the equipment behind it never notices. A difficult neighbor becomes a predictable one. And when the utility needs help, it becomes a useful one.

Interconnection changes, too. The utility certifies one medium-voltage box instead of untangling every transformer, UPS, chiller, pump, and switchgear lineup behind it. Engineers swap chip generations without a fresh interconnection study. Months come off the permitting timeline.

Inside the fence, UPS rooms become compute or cooling space. Density per construction dollar climbs.

And the economics flip. Equipment that runs at medium voltage, sits outside, and stores its own energy can qualify for tax credits, and earn revenue in grid programs like peak shaving and demand response. Backup power stops being insurance and starts paying for itself.

### **The architecture test**

In early 2026, we tested a full-scale system at the National Laboratory of the Rockies, a U.S. Department of Energy facility and the only place in the Western Hemisphere that can replicate real grid faults and AI-scale load swings concurrently in the same loop.

We hit it from both directions: real AI load profiles hit the compute side at full medium voltage. Grid faults hit the utility side, including a full zero-voltage event. The compute side didn’t flinch. Neither did the grid side. It cleared the large-load voltage ride-through requirements from the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), the grid operator, with room to spare.

Those rules exist because operators no longer take facilities this size on faith, and more are coming. Most of the industry treats them as hurdles. A medium-voltage, inline system clears them out of the box. Compliance isn’t an added feature. It’s what the architecture does.

### **The new layer**

Much of what looks like a grid problem in the AI buildout sits inside the fence, in equipment sized for a load that no longer exists. Move the right pieces up, out, and into the path, and a grid liability becomes a grid asset. Density goes up. Permitting time comes down. Backup power earns its keep.

The engineering works—and the next wave of AI factories is being built on it. The industry hasn’t named this layer yet. We call it the medium-voltage AI UPS. The name matters less than the choice: those factories can arrive as a strain on the grid or as strength for it. We already know how to build the second kind.

*This content was produced by ON.energy. It was not written by MIT Technology Review’s editorial staff.*

entries.title: 开发者用 Claude 一小时复刻 Win3.1 程序管理器，可在 Win11 和 macOS 上运行
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，如果你想在 Windows 11 或 macOS 设备上快速回味一把复古 Windows 体验，这款主打氛围感还原的 Windows 3.1 程序管理器复刻版或许会合你心意。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/18933296-fa00-4a32-b3ab-5f0ffed128ed.jpg?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

开发者 Mayuki 推出了一个精巧的怀旧小项目 ReProgman—— 名字源自早年 Windows 3.1 的核心系统外壳程序“progman.exe”，三十年前 Windows 95 问世后，这款程序管理器就彻底退出了历史舞台。

ReProgman 的还原度相当高，在发布 ReProgman 的社交动态里，Mayuki 写道：“我让 Claude 做了一个 Windows 3.1 程序管理器的复刻版”，“我觉得你大概能对着它怀旧个 30 秒吧。”

Claude Code 生成这款 Windows 3.1 外壳复刻版的速度相当快。仅用约一小时就产出的初版“效果已经不错”，但还需要花些功夫打磨细节、修复问题。而 Mayuki 自己也调侃，实际用 ReProgman 操作大概半分钟，就会觉得没意思了。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/e34a4e4e-80fb-463b-90c9-a104debebe3d.jpg?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

面向普通用户的 ReProgman 正式版体积在 12 到 16MB 之间，下载毫无负担，而且无需安装，点开就能运行。想体验的时候，用它带着怀旧感浏览当前系统里的程序和文件，完全不费事。Mayuki 表示，编译和运行这款程序需要.NET SDK 10.0 及以上版本。项目代码已在 GitHub 上以 MIT 开源协议发布。

总的来说，Mayuki 的这款 ReProgman 带来了一趟轻松的个人计算怀旧之旅，能带你重回上世纪 90 年代早中期的 Windows 3.X 时代。不过也有人认为，要体验复古计算的乐趣，不如在真实硬件上运行原汁原味的 MS-DOS / Windows 3.1 组合。IT之家注意到，今年 4 月，就有技术爱好者在搭载锐龙 9 9900X 处理器和 RTX 5060 Ti 显卡的顶级现代硬件上，以裸机模式成功运行了 Windows 3.1X。

  and maturity docs into a new `Contributing` tab; the Help tab's Testing group
  moves there too, beside `reference/test`.

  `Codex runtime reference`, `Plugin maintainer reference` -> `Plugin internals`,

- Order `Technical reference` so the cost pages and the session pages sit
  together, and land `openclaw-agent-runtime` there next to
  `agent-runtime-architecture` instead of in the end-user Install tab.
- Re-file pages that sat away from their siblings: `cli/devices` ->
  Tools and execution, `reference/device-models` and `platforms/mac/remote` ->
  the macOS app Setup group, `web/urls` after `web/dashboard-architecture`,
  `announcements/bluebubbles-imessage` -> the iMessage group, `prose` ->
  Install > Maintenance > Migrating, `start/hubs` + `start/docs-directory` ->
  Get started > Overview.
- Group the two retired-workspace-file migration pages under a
  `Retired workspace files` sub-group and pull the orphaned

- Add five orphaned pages to the nav: `channels/qa-channel`, `concepts/mantis`,
  `concepts/mantis-slack-desktop-runbook`, `specs/codex-supervision`,
  `plugins/reference/anthropic-vertex`.
- Rename Get started > `Guides` to `Setup guides and reference`.

Page structure
- automation/tasks: promote the CLI-reference and cross-system accordions to
  H3 headings so they appear in the outline (anchor stubs for the two titles
  whose pipes would have changed the slug).
- automation/imap: give the sender-bound-token and freshness rules their own H3.

这个方案以 NFC 文创玩偶为载体，轻触即秒级唤醒、零下载零注册；联动主管单位、景区与合规商户提供权威推荐，集成导览讲解、智能问答、路线规划、食宿优选、行程规划，实现从「人找服务」到「服务找人」，并可复制到博物馆、古街、非遗展馆等文旅场景。

三个行业领域的落地路径各有不同，但这是一种「通用智能体框架+专业Skills」的落地范式：通用能力做底座，行业知识做纵深，元景数字员工作为统一入口串联起从通用办公到专业场景的完整能力谱系。

好用不好用，试过才知道

测试前我最好奇的问题是：智能体帮人干活的爽感从何而来？几轮实测下来，答案变得具体了。

它虽然还不能「一句话改变世界」，但稳定可靠的程度已经积累出了信任。丢一句需求过去，AI 能自己把搜索、分析、做图、写报告这一长串流程跑完；定时任务每天准时把筛选好的日报推到微信，中途遇到弹窗、判错也能自己绕开、自己修正；换到写公文、画电气图、做文旅导览这些专业活儿，也都接得住。

总的来说，用得越久，越能体会到省心：它已经像是一个不用盯着、也不会掉链子的得力助手了。

当然，AI 工具光看测评是不够的，顺不顺手只有真实任务用上去才知道。好在元景数字员工一键安装、开箱即用，尝试的门槛并不高。

* 元景数字员工官网：<https://www.yjworker.10010.com/>

如果你也正被一堆重复琐碎的工作占着时间，不妨亲自上手试一试，让「数字员工」先帮你干一天活，剩下的，你自己会有答案！

entries.title: 国家级顶流AI赛事再开战！第三届「兴智杯」报名开启，等你来战
entries.content:
关注PK 2026-09-10 19:36 北京

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=c3d2c791&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2F5L8bhP5dIqFZl9ORON3NWanDEqvE3NIZPPodfYqGOcHkB5LrJKkY0NxeibH14iaea698SemREZOHKrc61oWpfWibZYkfJOnUadr2W3TZokP3q8%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

速来揭榜！

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=97ed75af&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FKmXPKA19gW889cR13aBX42evqQIRibKlicoCrHPEpT0tQiceNphESCa2eJTqstP8G0yqMTkeMFrOGue6kOyCKdTkA%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

编辑｜SIA

这个变化的发生速度，比很多人预想的更快。

2026 年 5 月，Anthropic 披露内部合并进入代码库的代码中，超过 80% 已经由 Claude 编写。与 2024 年相比，2026 年第二季度其典型工程师每天合并的代码量提升到了约 8 倍。

6 月，华为云披露，智果 AgentArts 企业级智能体平台面对真实生产级长程任务，端到端任务完成率提升至 80% ，会话级隔离记忆召回准确率达 90% ，推动智能体从「能做 Demo」走向真实生产环境；码道 CodeArts 代码智能体已支持代码生成、研发知识问答、单元测试用例生成、专家技能 Skills、Codebase 代码库索引、规范驱动开发等业界最新 AI Coding 技术，帮助开发者提高研发效率、优化编码体验。

与此同时，工程师的角色也在发生变化，从亲自完成每一步实现，逐渐转向定义目标、拆解问题、审查结果和处理异常。

这种变化已经不只发生在软件开发领域。

6 月，Cadence 发布具备全自主能力的 ChipStack AI Super Agent 。它可以围绕规格理解、RTL 生成、验证规划、仿真、调试等任务自主决定下一步动作并持续迭代。

Cadence 称，在相关验证场景中，原本可能持续数周的流程可以被压缩到一天以内。到了 7 月，类似的 Agent 能力又进一步延伸到了 PCB 和先进封装设计。

我们正在跨过 AI 发展的另一个分水岭。过去，它更像一个被动响应的工具；今天，它正在变成一个主动执行者。

从 Chatbot 到 Reasoner 再到 Agent；从生成内容到操作软件、设计芯片，再到进入机器人和物理世界，「 AI 能力曲线」正在快速上扬。但另一边，却是相对滞后的「组织与经济曲线」。

斯坦福大学《 2026 AI Index 》显示，全球受访组织中的AI整体采用率已攀升至88%；但真正部署 AI Agent 的比例，在绝大多数业务职能中仍然只有个位数。

最新一轮麦肯锡全球人工智能现状调查发现，真正从 AI 中获得显著价值的企业，与普通企业最大的差异之一，在于有没有重新设计工作流程。

接近四分之三的 AI 高绩效企业表示，他们已经因为 AI 而对工作流程进行了根本性重构；其他企业这一比例只有约四分之一。

这意味着，人才培养、产业体系、应用融合、生态构建等问题，正制约着 AI 真正进入企业流程。如何让前沿 AI 能力跨过工程化、场景化和规模化应用的门槛，把技术能力真正转化为产业价值，正成为 AI 下一阶段真正值得解决的问题。

正是在这一背景下，第三届「兴智杯」全国人工智能创新应用大赛（以下简称「大赛」）吹响新的集结号。

大赛由中国信息通信研究院、深圳市人工智能产业办公室、深圳市龙岗区人民政府共同举办，并于 8 月 31 日在深圳市龙岗区机器人剧场正式启动。大赛以「兴智赋能，云创未来」为主题，旨在持续推进人工智能核心技术的创新突破，促进前沿领域技术研究的工程化落地应用，加快中国人工智能产业走深向实。

作为**我国规模最大、参赛人数最多、参赛主体最丰富的国家级人工智能专业赛事**，「兴智杯」始终紧密贴合产业发展的实际节奏与阶段性热点，坚持「**与产业同频，适度超前布局**」。

历届赛题的演进，犹如一部浓缩的中国 AI 产业发展史。

早在 2022 至 2023 年的首届大赛期间，赛事就敏锐捕捉到了深度学习向大模型跃迁的前夜，将焦点锚定在预训练模型与多模态等前沿技术底座上。

到了 2025 年的第二届大赛，面对生成式 AI 的全面爆发，赛事紧跟多模态融合与智能体的快速突破，大力推动了大模型与 Agent 应用的创新探索。

随着人工智能迈向自主智能、具身智能和 AI 原生的新纪元，第三届大赛将核心视野精准对齐于「 AI 能否自主完成任务、深入物理世界，并形成规模化的产业价值」。

在见证 AI 技术「三级跳」的同时，「兴智杯」也发展成连接技术创新、产业应用、人才培养与生态协同的重要平台。

从首届吸引 1.63 万余人、9000 余支团队报名，到第二届参与人数突破 1.8 万余人，赛事的足迹已覆盖我国（除台湾省外）全部省级行政区，并吸引了来自美、加、新、意等海外多国的顶尖开发者同台竞技。

大赛不仅曾获得 ITU AI/ML Challenge 中国区赛事的官方主办授权，还深度融入并推动了国家级开源社区的繁荣建设，其全球影响力和号召力日益凸显。

在「兴智杯」的赛场上，既有高校和科研机构围绕模型、算法和关键技术持续攻坚，也有 AI 头部企业和创新先锋探索新的产品形态与技术边界。与此同时，来自制造、能源、通信、金融、交通等传统行业的企业，也带着真实业务问题和产业需求进入赛场。

高校、科研机构、科技企业、传统行业企业，不再各自寻找答案，而是在同一个赛场上，让前沿技术与真实问题直接碰撞。

值得一提的是，本届大赛进一步汇聚高水平行业资源，成立了由院士顾问领衔、主席团专家以及专家组成的专家委员会。上百位来自产、学、研、金融领域的权威专家将齐聚一堂，为参赛团队提供从宏观方向把控、底层技术攻坚，到最终商业成果落地的全链路闭环指导。

**三大主题+云智专项的硬核挑战，等你来战**

本届大赛设置**技术创新、行业赋能、生态协同三大主题赛**，以及**云智应用专项赛**和**总决赛**。

各主题赛下设若干具体赛题，主要分为技术模型赛和解决方案赛两类。

技术模型赛主要聚焦具体技术问题，重点看参赛团队能否通过算法、模型和代码实现取得更优效果。参赛作品形式为代码实现方案。

解决方案赛主要面向真实、复杂的行业场景，重点看能否形成一套可落地、见成效、可复制推广的解决办法。参赛作品形式为行业解决方案。

（一）主题赛一：技术创新

主题赛以国产软硬件底座为基础，围绕当前人工智能发展的共性关键技术进行创新，鼓励前沿交叉领域的探索性研究。

设置了**三道技术模型赛：大模型智能体关键能力技术创新赛、小分子药物预测技术创新赛、Agent 驱动的机械臂应用技术创新赛**。

重点考察模型自主规划、工具调用、多步骤推理、科学计算、预测泛化，以及机器人感知、决策与执行等关键能力，推动人工智能由通用生成向自主执行、科学发现和物理世界作业进一步拓展。

**（二）主题赛二：行业赋能（「AI+ 」）**

主赛题联合行业头部企业与新型研发机构，围绕**工业、医疗、信息通信、金融、电子信息、园区管理**等国民经济关键领域设置赛题，坚持由真实产业需求和一线痛点出题。

参赛方案面对的不只是模型指标，还要考虑安全、实时性、合规、精度、可靠性，甚至现有业务流程到底能不能接得住。因此，这一主赛题尤其强调三个「真实」：**真实场景、真实约束、真实成效**。

「通关」方案最终不仅要解决问题，还需要通过实际测试或试点验证，证明效果可量化、价值可验证，并具备进一步复制推广的可能。

**（三）主题赛三：生态协同**

如果算力、芯片、数据、工程系统和产业生态跟不上，再强的模型也很难真正成为生产力，中国信通院基于人工智能软硬件协同创新与适配验证中心开展的 AISHPerf 国模国芯适配测试结果表明，当前国产算力已能够较好适配主流开源模型，具备支撑上层应用创新和推理服务能力。因此，主题赛聚焦于构建自主可靠、协同高效、开放繁荣的人工智能产业生态，且**均为解决方案赛**。

* 通过「**智算集群工程化**」与「**国模国芯应用**」赛题，要求参赛者深入真实场景，推进集群调度与底层软硬件适配，让算力化为稳定可靠的生产力
* 设立「词元（Token）服务应用」与「OPC（单人 AI 创业）」两大赛题，聚焦大模型时代的新技术、新业态与新模式。前者重点探索精准计量与算力经济学，推动构筑全栈自主可控的底层生态；后者开放探索 AI 降低创新创业门槛、释放个体创新活力的新模式。

**（四）专项赛题：云智应用**

在当前 AI 技术迭代持续加速，企业智能化转型需要构建「具备更低成本、更高安全、更快迭代」特征的智能化底座。华为云围绕 Agentic AI 构筑差异化服务, 为本届赛事提供云上工具平台，专家资源，让团队能够在真实的云智环境里解决真实的行业问题。

专项赛设置七**道解决方案赛题，**推动 AI 从单点能力向云端协同、流程嵌入和安全可控的规模化应用演进，形成一批可运行、可验证、可复制推广的云智融合标杆。它们分别是：

* **面向代码生成的生产效率创新：**鼓励开发者依托华为云码道（ CodeArts ）等代码平台，重构需求拆解、代码编写到测试验证的全链路，证明 AI 对生产效能的颠覆。
* **AI 数据湖与治理：**要求选手打通多模态数据的治理闭环，用高质量数据彻底释放 AI 价值。
* **垂直大模型：鼓励选手使用华为盘古大模型等通用模型底座，与行业专属数据深度融合，淬炼出真正「懂行」的业务利器。**
* 具身智能：让 AI 进入物理世界，真正完成现实环境中的任务。

* **城市智能云**：探索 AI 如何进一步进入城市治理与公共服务场景。

* **企业级流程智能体**：鼓励选手使用华为云智果（ AgentArts ）等企业级智能体平台，深度嵌入制造、金融、政务等行业高频业务场景，重塑运营范式。

* **智能体全生命周期安全管控**：当 Agent 拥有越来越大的自主权，如何确保它始终安全、可靠、可控。

**赛事福利：多维激励、全周期护航**

（一）大赛奖项

各主题赛将评选**一等奖、二等奖、三等奖**，并从优秀团队中确定晋级大赛总决赛的名单；总决赛通过答辩评审，最终评选出**一等奖、二等奖、三等奖及优胜奖**。

（二）获胜项目激励

「兴智杯」不仅是技术竞技场，更是一个为选手精准匹配商业资源的孵化器。

* **合作对接：大赛将直接促成优质项目与金融机构展开投资洽谈合作。同时，官方会面向供需两侧提供精准对接渠道。**
* **政策支持：官方明确将为企业或人才落地提供资金、场地、落户等高含金量支持。此外，还有区域差异化配套或项目支持政策，极大降低早期创业与试错成本。**
* **人才通道：针对求职或寻求更好职业发展的技术极客，大赛直接提供行业领军企业热门岗位的招聘绿色通道。**
* **宣传与荣誉：优胜项目不仅能获得官方颁发的奖杯加证书作为高优背书，大赛还会联动高端媒体、知名科技媒体等多渠道进行高强度宣传曝光。最顶尖的方案将被收录进《第三届「兴智杯」全国人工智能创新应用大赛优秀项目案例集》进行集中推介。**

**赛程安排**

大赛包括**主题赛初赛**、**主题赛决赛**和**大赛总决赛**三个阶段。其中，主题赛初赛以线上形式开展，各主题赛决赛视实际情况另行安排。

预计于 2026 年 12 月在深圳市龙岗区举行大赛总决赛暨颁奖典礼相关活动。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=02bcc5f1&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2F5L8bhP5dIqG9xvKgdzTkYQ4PibcEIliaiaDlJ1bsqTM6IFYlLLXB1rFl5gEHuov1uUqoR7lRc7nwuYrkvbreHdq1RKic8jd7abRBBibnG5vb2bdQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**报名方式**

（一）谁可以报名？

大赛面向国内外人工智能创新力量开放，个人和团队均可报名参赛。

无论是企业及开发者团队、高校师生、科研机构研究人员，还是跨行业探索 AI 创新应用的团队与个人，都可以结合相应赛题方向报名参赛。

（二）资源支持

大赛举办期间，将为参赛者提供必要的算力基础资源保障，部分赛题开放高质量数据与大模型资源池。

依托集报名、线上评测、代码提交与活动直播于一体的一站式服务平台，彻底扫除开发者的后顾之忧。

上大赛官网，了解大赛详情：<http://www.aiinnovation.com.cn>

参赛者均须通过大赛官网注册报名，截止时间以官网公布时间为准。

About us

entries.title: 软件维护是笔“长期税”！Codex负责人：Agent正在打掉这笔账，程序员最费时间的工作要变了
entries.content:
原创 姜篇 2026-09-10 17:50 日本

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=048a07db&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2FZhxqo7xEfgIy8WP3ZoIpu7YreNdCMrmRFTC1DHoicOXmM0Dic0QeCM60NnvI5crzEFTU1oWv1hoZM05QKkpCnwJp9XRaGDpf6d9TuS9XhZMa4%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

软件维护是笔“长期税”！Codex负责人：Agent正在打掉这笔账，程序员最费时间的工作要变了

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=b6a4647d&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FMOwlO0INfQoIDJ0nx1IhNibpIpYLrpUE0kIP9qbF1iaY7EoZpaic6IojvbXibd5ZGiatxmjtibQRcVbGAPM9Ijvp66yQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=59e2cfe8&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgK7edic5Mic1Chh98qDHAgbIXaqbRicdJWCA4dfUicYa0Glp727Tw5bdJ0j7bypp8gOjHaVYXH8q6GG2dqsibsSiaKniaviaJR4zoyGUib4%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

编辑 | 姜篇

> Tibo：“Maintenance is ... a tax.”
>
> Tibo：“维护就像一笔持续支付的税。”

对开发者来说，这笔“税”一点都不抽象。

功能上线只是一次性开支，后面的每一次修改维护，都是一笔账单。

Tibo认为，Coding Agent会先改变这部分账单。大量令人拖延的维护工作，会被Agent代替。

备注：Tibo是Codex早期创建者之一，如今负责OpenAI核心产品与平台，Codex也在他的管理范围内。

最近的一场访谈中，他聊了Rust、开源、模型、代码审查、系统重构和Codex与ChatGPT的合并。

Tibo还反复提到一个容易被忽略的部分：模型只提供推理能力，决定Agent能否进入真实项目的，是包在模型外面的harness。

这些话题看起来很散，放到一起却指向同一件事：**OpenAI并不只想让Codex更会写代码，而是想让它进入软件的整个生命周期。**

**![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=3c8a286f&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgKSdBYAFz1uHIx0Puz0OLvlH1QLs8MBiaQc040qsvXia5nDgAk4Ydm68RFEHj1icCzibQVZO6WE2IbvX5luoQE5vjhAy12VjNBAnOA%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)**

***Tibo认为，维护仍然必要，但其中很多步骤会被自动化***

**以下为访谈内容，我们进行了翻译与整理。**

## **软件写完只是开始，贵的是以后每一次修改**

Tibo举了一个最直接的例子，依赖升级。

> Tibo：“只要更新版本号、读懂变更日志，再根据代码判断影响，这类任务完全可以自动化。”

以前，团队往往会把这类工作一拖再拖。

它不会直接带来新功能，却可能打破构建、引入兼容问题，还要补测试和准备回滚。很多技术债，就是从一句“下个迭代再处理”开始的。

当Agent可以读变更日志、搜索全仓库、修改调用点、运行测试并继续修错，这笔小账开始变得好算。开发者不用一个文件一个文件地搬迁，而是先给它一个明确终点：哪些测试必须通过，哪些行为不能变，哪些目录不允许碰。

但“自动维护”有一个前提。Tibo特意提到了写得清楚的变更日志和文档。一个没有测试、没有边界、连启动命令都要靠老员工口口相传的项目，换成再强的模型也不会突然好维护。

## **Codex开始接触的，是整个项目**

OpenAI内部给了一个很直观的使用场景。

> Tibo：“Have you asked Codex?”
>
> Tibo：“你问过Codex吗？”

新员工想知道一个项目进展到哪，谁在处理某个问题，以及当初为什么做了某个技术决定，同事会先让他去问Codex。原因也很直接：它已经接上了Slack、文档和代码。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=a6ee3b61&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgISz2fsax4x4W59O2fAcYqn7vykbn1xKYKAxaVgKKJe9xIaSiaWmicziaLmSCAsM25EXicSEopGO9ozOArXHVH8hhicYNGAEzWOMLRQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Codex在OpenAI内部已经接入沟通记录、文档和代码*

这和在编辑器里点一次“补全”完全是两件事。

当Agent只能看当前文件，它是一个代码生成器。当它能追查需求来源、查历史讨论、读接口文档、运行命令并查看日志，它才开始参与项目。

开发团队会很快碰到一个现实问题：你是否愿意让Agent读到这么多东西？

接入越广，Agent越了解项目；接入越广，权限和数据风险也越集中。公开频道、可搜索的决策记录、分级权限和操作日志，不再是文档团队的“卫生工作”，它们直接决定Agent能不能进入真实研发流程。

## **Agent能不能干活，模型只决定了一半**

Tibo花了不少时间讲harness。这是整场访谈中最值得开发者细看的一部分。

> Tibo：“The harness ... is always a little bit ahead.”
>
> Tibo：“harness总会比模型往前多走一小步。”

Harness要把上下文、工具、安全边界、开发者指令和反馈循环装起来，再把模型放进去。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=5acaaad0&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJq0zjOItAdhCkvXS5Yr8BZibasftib4yHRVUgsnnTyQVmPSwicVnT2dfrkVQia3hmGYbBapicU0LU1179U2vIsPRjhnVVJw08VaAVg%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*当模型还不够稳定时，harness用工具、规则和反馈提高可靠性*

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=27d8efc4&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgJob0duDo6mJ62cTU1vKib73bmtZ10iaS8ceeNdVHHAiav2nBMCfm6oqxibyHBzALs9dwJopm95Nr41d8IlPkzdVQovHW5AibibZcF7I%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*模型提供推理能力，harness负责把它变成可执行、可检查的工程过程*

OpenAI团队每天都要做一个取舍：某个缺陷是应该改harness，还是等模型本身升级？

> Tibo：“如果模型一个月后就能修好，也许不必写上万行代码去绕过它的缺陷。”

这对企业自建Agent同样适用。不要遇到模型失败，就继续叠加提示词、规则和分支逻辑。先把问题归类：是上下文没给到，工具返回不稳定，验收条件不清楚，还是模型确实不会。这四类问题，修法完全不同。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=0c5cd83a&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgIqpempUBoC2yarMiaeXgmtz3VwAkXFuQBlRgibOJYqqfricibjUuAz6Qrm5o2cwjUjrEWw1rYq1ia5SoxBj9MPLfSyoENlJNZb2KNY%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Codex Agent循环，Agent会在工具结果和模型判断之间反复迭代*

## **Codex为什么开源，还允许接入其他模型**

Codex CLI开源时，Tibo的理由很简单：他们正在做一个会改代码的Agent，早晚会让它反过来改自己。如果代码对社区开放，开发者可以直接参与，OpenAI也能从真实使用中学到东西。

> Tibo：“如果你在做一个优秀的编程harness，为什么一定要把它和某个模型绑死？”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=d3922fea&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJQoEa3oTup782G4Gk55licibAdxsJuKFR9cyZQZeZRicMSxJVsGKdvTZVw8qeOebmRXvJSv6uDhjWn6vZISbYpYjmc7B8VdKxD3M%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Tibo认为，编程harness不必与单一模型供应商绑定*

这句话决定了Codex的一个重要边界：它可以是OpenAI产品，底层harness却不必只服务OpenAI模型。

对开发团队来说，这比“又多一个模型可选”重要得多。

模型会迭代，价格会变，限额和合规条件也会变。如果任务编排、工具接入、验收规则和历史记录都只能跟着一家模型走，团队换模型的成本会非常高。

真正值得留在自己手里的，是任务记录、评测集、权限边界、工具协议和可回放的执行日志。这些东西能带着走，模型才是真的可替换。

## **代码审查不会消失，逐行找错正在失去价值**

> Tibo：“The role of code review is changing.”
>
> Tibo：“代码审查的作用正在改变。”

Tibo早期参与过Codex的代码审查模型。

他说，模型已经能沿着依赖向下追三四层，去查一个第三方库的真实实现，再判断文档里的承诺是否和代码一致。这类问题，人工审查往往要花几个小时，甚至只有熟悉那个库的人才能看出来。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=af041a97&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgKNzeCibuKNIvKKSVic5lkGhgHdNXZCdXLpw2kumqL5pafOzw7TU02Iwff2klQ327aKFPxGe9Z314ichWWzKIvOOjYqz2Ticsozjb8%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*模型可以追踪多层依赖，帮人找出逻辑、正确性和安全问题*

那人还审什么？

看意图。这次修改是否真的解决用户问题，有没有为了跑绿测试而绕开需求，是否引入了团队不愿意承受的长期复杂度。

看证据。测试通过是否足够，有没有需要看压测、监控指标、历史数据回放和灰度结果。

看责任。这个改动如果在生产环境出问题，谁能叫停，怎样撤回，怎样定位数据影响。

审查不会少，审查对象会从一串diff，扩大到整个任务的证据链。

## **一百个Agent涌入仓库，架构反而更重要**

有一种看法认为，代码可以随时重写后，模块、文档和架构都没那么重要了。Tibo给出的场景恰好相反。

> Tibo：“以前一个项目可能要一年才扩到50到100名工程师，现在100个Agent一个周末就可能进来。”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=eb9ce52a&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJG4fQ5YcqPtqCyYLfLhE0dMFM4IfdRibmredkfm5pu2WIBSy21jezKPCyGzOdM4FGXZB0kj4ibX6xju7E5gX9scs6nKHeETpGRg%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Agent让项目的“贡献者数量”在很短时间内暴涨*

人类团队缓慢扩张时，大家还有时间补文档、分拆模块、约定接口。Agent涌入的速度快得多，原本可以晚点再补的工程规矩，一开始就得在。

否则，一个Agent在改鉴权，一个Agent在换数据结构，第三个Agent根据旧接口补测试。它们都很勤快，也都可能在局部正确。最后需要人收拾的，却是一个无法合并的仓库。

团队要提前写清服务边界、模块所有权、接口契约、禁止修改区域和合并顺序。每个Agent使用独立分支或worktree，用契约测试卡住跨模块改动，才能让并行不变成冲突。

Tibo还谈到了更大的系统重构。

过去需要数年的改造，有了Agent后可能大幅加速。但重构变快，不代表可以随便改。迁移路径、兼容期、数据校验和回退策略只会变得更重要。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=2487efce&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgK7otDHY9mkGocib6euJAibNDz9BKftB6Ogs4A1gSlEzbxibQOzEqaMC6zn6ztP1S8RRETAxYdlSRXNgZDTMUKuDibTBMKwWsL4aRQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*团队依靠Agent和工程约束持续扩展代码库*

## **Codex与ChatGPT走到一起，目标是把本地Agent推向云端**

Codex起初是一套本地工具，可以直接读仓库、跑终端、改文件。ChatGPT则是一套托管在云端、面向大规模用户的产品。Tibo说，合并的难点恰恰来自这两套完全不同的技术栈。

> Tibo：“问题是，如何保留本地Coding Agent的能力，又把它做成能服务更多人的产品。”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=a750dfe2&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgIWg2a75nnhibOJb9tXq13GkItZXTPzZzV3NSJ8jibEBrVDw4xXzS4QEzV2Ea6zl7QKGXmnqLscbpNuvRmUaB98AoWBIhh6O6sUQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Codex与ChatGPT的融合，需要把本地Agent能力放进可扩展的云端环境*

这一步做成后，Codex的工作对象就不再局限于开发者当前打开的电脑。任务可以在云端持续运行，中途保留状态，必要时再把人叫回来。

> Tibo：自己会把白天没有想完的大问题交给Codex，让它过夜调查，第二天早上再看结果。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=8a27e3fc&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJw2e86iacwGPVCAqCUSee8ZqhXYnWvruBUPvOh2EQic4T1BUYxsHxMwgxJq873ojicibjMq39tMibryt82fcUwg3L8HGcerL23zWSI%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Codex的任务开始从几分钟的修改，延长到可以持续一整夜的调查*

这也是为什么OpenAI在做的已经不止是一个CLI。一个要长时间运行、并行处理任务、接入企业资料和工具的Agent，需要计算环境、任务队列、权限、快照、日志和回滚。它的形状已经越来越像研发基础设施。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=87ae4bd5&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgLgoZ0xxicWdMwZ5miaIb60WMEbgibUQeQMhE9JQnWBZxkHZ3ZaU0LfYyibo3cLkibTo0ibNzZ8d7jibJKp59DuM3YsnPwmVjGKVTN9nI%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*同一套harness可以服务CLI、IDE和Web等多种客户端*

## **评论区：有人从Claude转向Codex，也有人追着问“为什么停不下来”**

Tibo这期访谈的评论区里，讨论很快从“请再重置一次额度”转向了工具信任。

一位用户反馈，他在macOS版ChatGPT里中途取消提示后，Agent循环没有快速停止，原提示也无法编辑。

这类问题看起来只是交互瑕疵，放进长时间Agent任务里就会变成控制问题：人发出停止指令后，系统必须真的停下来。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=83659bea&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgLE8ab8hVuTQtYPXvPgiazVmgu8388ibXSApcOaiaquN9PMRUicUaC5P8P7gsY6ysv24tbqYGXs7ocHrTibDK7QGVicMTPdP5zAM9v5Y%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*YouTube用户反馈，中途取消任务后Agent循环没有快速停止*

另一位用户说，他曾经因Codex变慢转向Claude，如今又更信任Codex团队的开放程度和沟通方式。这也说明，开发者选编程Agent时，已经不只看一次榜单，还会看速度、额度、开源程度和团队的响应。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=d22f8b81&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgI7elSb0yaokt14gg6YfanLO1WSpFT14oQaoUexA2eRF9MTic07yhAl45d0YHqfE8JceSic79pnaOuMBlXuSzVMictdic4UX7MViaLo%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*YouTube用户表示，自己会根据速度和信任在不同Coding Agent之间切换*

还有用户说，Tibo的产品方向和使用体验，让他从长期使用的Claude转向Codex。这是很明确的支持，但也提醒了一点：Agent成为基础设施后，用户信任的是整套工程系统，不是某一次漂亮的回答。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=78353f48&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgKpW6NvXYFkqL91TwuFDtFHLZcibzYy0FQMkS89vY7dhIjVTHyD89Dsv7Xmnib69zxJH2N6H2icUgnibnBhFibolEZW7jdyqoaS9vf8%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*YouTube用户评论，Tibo的产品方向促使他从Claude转向Codex*

## **写在最后**

Coding Agent最容易展示的能力，是几分钟写完一个功能。Tibo这次谈得更多的，却是功能写完以后的事。

依赖要升级，Bug要追，系统要重构，代码要审查，项目历史要查，一百个Agent同时改仓库时还要避免互相踩脚。

这些工作没有演示一段代码那么刺激，却占了软件生命周期的大部分。只要Agent开始稳定地接手这些事，它就不再只是写代码的工具。

那时候，团队真正要重做的，是一套能让Agent长期干活，同时又可以被人验收、限制和追责的软件工程系统。

entries.title: AI floods security teams with flaws — business context sets priorities
entries.content:
![Abstract grainy waves of pink, orange, purple, and blue flowing across a dark background.](https://cdn.thenewstack.io/media/2026/09/dd536670-resource-database-vvo9wc61vqe-unsplash-1024x819.jpg)

**A security researcher testing a 300-person B2B company** with a global footprint discovered an internet-exposed database with weak authentication during a routine scan. The database appeared to be a prime target for attackers; it had critical severity and was an obvious first-fix candidate. Upon further inspection, however, researchers learned it was a resettable test database used to test job candidates, rather than a system containing client data.

The episode represents a critical problem: Scanners and security researchers can’t infer the real cost of a compromise on their own. Increasingly, companies rely on an external partner to handle cloud vulnerability triage and keep teams from becoming overwhelmed. Scanners produce excessive noise, requiring focus and attention from engineers to understand alerts and complex attack techniques, tune out false positives, and work with teams on remediation, reducing the time they have to build new features, work with customers, or scale up their tech environment.

**Tech employees have more on their to-do lists than ever:** Product teams face an infinite stream of feature requests and engineering teams carry more technical debt than they can clear. When you factor in a reorg, many employees may have larger project scopes and leaner teams, all while constantly monitoring, correcting, and mentoring AI agents. Some reports cite [90-hour work weeks.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvgx4yd1gl2o)

Beyond today’s structural challenges, security teams are drowning in a different type of data. Programs absorb identity events, firewall logs, endpoint alerts, vendor feeds, and threat intelligence, producing far more analysis data than even a few years ago. Every item can look urgent, high-risk, and worthy of immediate attention. With finite hours, it’s hard to know where to act first.

[Jon Rose](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jrose400/), founder of the information security and risk management advisory firm [IOmergent](https://iomergent.com/),  has seen firsthand how AI and near-universal tooling are producing more findings than teams can triage.

“Within the span of security work, there’s an unending list of things you could tackle, and you’re pulled in so many different directions… But you have to be ruthless about prioritizing and investing your time.”

“Within the span of security work, there’s an unending list of things you could tackle, and you’re pulled in so many different directions,” Rose tells *The New Stack*. “But you have to be ruthless about prioritizing and investing your time.”  
  
The challenge, then, isn’t remediation. It’s allocation: Deciding where limited engineering and security capacity will make the greatest impact is the most important question security leaders answer every day. A technical severity score, used without threat and environmental context, cannot answer the business question: *What should we fix first?* Effective vulnerability prioritization turns raw findings into business-aware priorities, and that judgment is the real work.

## CVSS limitations: a starting point, not a decision

For security teams, a Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) provides a useful baseline. Its base metrics classify a vulnerability’s severity — attack vector, complexity, required privileges, and potential impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability. But a severity score is designed to be stable across environments, so it can’t tell a team whether an asset is exposed to the internet, shielded by compensating controls, or central to the business.

Essentially, treating a base severity score as an automatic fix-first ticket is problematic, rather than using CVSS on its own.

CVSS can include Threat and Environmental metrics that account for evolving exploit conditions and organization-specific context. However, risk-based vulnerability management still depends on accurate knowledge of the environment — and on someone applying that context consistently.

“The piece that’s missing from any of these tools is the grounding in the business, the understanding of what actually matters,” Rose says.

## Escalate the internet-facing medium

A smart decision framework deprioritizes the urgency of a score and probes reachability: whether an attacker could actually reach the vulnerable component.

“Is the affected service exposed to the public internet or not? Or is it isolated behind network controls and accessible only to a limited set of internal users?” Rose says. “Often, issues will get flagged, but it’s not in a position where it could be triggered.”

Next is consequence. An exposed flaw on a disposable test system might be a genuine security concern. Still, it doesn’t carry the same weight as a weakness on the application that processes customer transactions, stores sensitive information, or underpins a company’s main revenue stream. So while the severity might be alarming, the business outcome might not.

Teams should also ask whether the weakness is attracting active attacker interest and where it could lead. A vulnerability listed in [CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) catalog deserves urgent scrutiny, because there’s evidence of exploitation in the wild.

The Exploit Prediction Scoring System provides a forward-looking signal: An estimate of the likelihood that exploitation of a particular vulnerability will be observed over the next 30 days. Neither replaces a business decision, but both help distinguish a theoretical risk from one that demands attention now. However, as AI-driven exploitation accelerates, the window between what is known to be vulnerable and what is actively exploited is shrinking because the cost of building and weaponizing exploits is dropping.

The relevant attack path might also extend beyond the affected machine. A comparatively modest flaw can become an immediate concern if it provides a route into privileged accounts, a production system, or customer data. Conversely, a high-severity finding can be deprioritized — temporarily — if it is not reachable, has limited impact, and is protected by reliable controls.

“The speed and the depth of research and investigation into those security issues are going faster,” Rose says. “So it can change really quickly.” The worst state is unacknowledged risk sitting in the backlog. Even the best detection degrades when [no one owns the trend line](https://thenewstack.io/cloud-security-triage-cadence/). Teams should track exceptions, set review dates, and name an owner. Accepted risk is still risk; the difference is that it’s explicit, time-bound, and revisited.

## An operator capability, not a weekend project

Security teams are leaning more on AI to prioritize and triage threats, and they’re uncovering vulnerabilities at an unprecedented pace. Yet the sheer volume of findings is overwhelming, even for the most efficient of humans.

It’s clear, too, that AI can make it easier to discover less obvious paths to exploitation, and to introduce new ones. An academic study of 20,000+ issues fixed by AI found that LLMs introduce [nearly 9x as many new vulnerabilities as developers](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.02976v1), exhibiting unique patterns not found in developers’ code. The answer is to use AI at the outcome level. For every alert, the goal is to have the SOC analyst’s standard questions answered quickly: new or known, what’s exposed, what data is at risk, prod or dev, and how it has evolved.

> “Effective programs start by aligning with executive teams to understand the business — where the company is going — so allocation and adjustments track the actual risk, not just the score.”

“That’s how teams get thousands of alerts down to 10 to 20 prioritized tickets,” Rose tells *The New Stack*. “[Effective programs](https://iomergent.com/managed-cspm/?utm_source=tns&utm_campaign=tns-judgment) start by aligning with executive teams to understand the business — where the company is going — so allocation and adjustments track the actual risk, not just the score.”

As to-do lists grow ever longer, business-context judgment that’s applied every day by someone who owns it is something worth dedicating more resources.

***If you think you’d benefit from managed cloud security,*** [***book a 30-minute cloud security scoping call with IOmergent***](https://iomergent.com/managed-cspm/?utm_source=thenewstack&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=tns_sponsored_article_1&utm_content=underwater)***.***

The post [AI floods security teams with flaws — business context sets priorities](https://thenewstack.io/vulnerability-prioritization-business-context/) appeared first on [The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io).

entries.title: 对话更流畅，控车更懂你——超级小爱背后技术解读
entries.content:
小米技术 2026-09-10 18:05 北京

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=37ecbf5a&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2FrPSwicFZNl4aWxwVpO4Jt1Dd487hMk3bNvHvZqxEfYFYbl7dkF8OnMQBvEyRXdHTBicKlgXuqQhrHk1o6f1Xs3ibehdCaO5ZAePm4YKeys5jdc%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

日常用车时，你也许遇到过这些场景：出门自驾，行李塞了满满一车；周末郊游，朋友们想在车上打牌；露营的夜晚，想在车上找到最佳的观景休息模式；导航规划到一半，想顺路买点其他东西……

这些关于车内空间的智能编排需求，背后却涉及座椅、空调、灯光、导航、娱乐等多个系统的联动。在小米澎程上，这些复杂的跨系统协作被交给了超级小爱专家模式——你用一句话描述想要的场景，会客厅、休息舱、极致储物间，编排、规划、执行全部由小爱完成。

而让超级小爱真正做到“说一句就搞定”的背后，是两项核心技术的升级：快慢系统和全双工对话。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=97130f64&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FrPSwicFZNl4YtH9P1FdeYiceibKFchKnTzv8tNZOvn57zLDL2gkWhqEGPMcRHcY9sqQUiaibank0z6vrVpZ5DPvMmfQs8lY8yNPwuUCya6Y4VIiak%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**01**

### **快慢系统：更智能的分流算法**

一次自然流畅的车载对话，要做到两件事：响应要快，结果要对。

很多时候，这两件事却像天平的两端——想让助手“想得更清楚”，就得让它多思考一会，用户会觉得慢；想让助手“回得更快"，跳过深度思考，结果就可能没那么准。

因此我们需要组合两个不同的系统，来解决这个问题。快系统负责快速、直觉和自动化反应，慢系统负责理性、分析和深度思考。

**********▍**************把对的请求，送到对的链路****

快慢系统的核心思路很朴素：**不同复杂度的请求，不该走同一条处理链路。**

快系统执行速度快、成本低，承接“打开空调”“音量调大”“导航到公司”这类高频简单请求。慢系统能力强，承接多途经点导航、条件筛选搜索、长程任务编排这类需要深度推理的复杂请求。

快慢系统的目标，就是把每一个请求分发到效率最高的链路上，在满足度、延时、成本之间找到平衡。

同样以“导航”开头，两句话走的却是完全不同的两条路：“导航到公司”语义明确、操作单一，你刚说完指令，路线规划就开始；而“找一个能看见长江的露营地，最好停车免费且附近两公里有商场可以吃饭”，则被智能分流到慢系统，理解模糊语义、筛选多个条件、规划完整行程。

**********▍******************更快更准的回复********

******我们来举个例子，“找一个能看见长江的露营地，最好停车免费，附近两公里有商场可以吃饭” ，这个指令包含了地点周边信息的筛选需求，它需要理解模糊语义、筛选多个条件、调用多个工具才能规划完整的行程。******

******这种复杂请求，得交给深度思考。为了让复杂请求“想得清楚、又回得快”，这次我们基于 Xiaomi MiMo 模型做了两项关键升级：******

1. 第一步，我们做了一个关键调整：把模型从“边想边答”（think模式）切换到了“直接作答”（no-think模式）。这一切换带来了非常显著的响应提速——模型耗时**平均下降了约****35%**。大家的直观的感受是：小爱“利索多了”。但跳过思考，复杂任务的准确度会下降。面对多途经点、条件筛选的导航需求，模型更容易“想岔”或“漏工具”。
2. 第二步，也是关键一步：Xiaomi MiMo **模型引入****RAG-Planning 。就像人在考试时，如果手边有几道类似的例题，就能快速照着做出正确判断。RAG-Planning 在小爱开始处理你的问题之前，先从知识库里检索出几个“类似问题的完整解题思路”，作为示例喂给模型。这样模型不需要从头推理，而是参考类似解法快速做出准确判断——相当于开卷考试，速度和准确率同时提升。**

加入 RAG-Planning 之后，小爱的任务完成度和可用率得到了大幅度提升，更重要的是，它守住了速度这条底线：相比之前的 think 版本，端到端耗时依旧保持 no-think 的低时延，最快能快出3到6秒，这在车载场景里，是你能实实在在感知到的差距。

**对 Xiaomi MiMo 的这一轮优化，让****小爱****用 no-think 的速度，做到了 think 模式的准确度。**

**02**

### **全双工对话：边听边说的自然交流**

你正让小爱“导航去东湖落雁景区”，话没说完又插一句“空调调到24度”。小爱先立刻执行空调，等这句播完，它记着导航还没完成，接着补上路线规划。

这一次超级小爱全双工升级，我们把拒识、判停和打断放进同一个控制模块里统一决策，让小爱持续感知车内对话状态，同步判断三件事：你是不是想和它说话、你有没有说完、此刻要不要中断播报。

小爱的对话能力从“听完再说”变成“边听边说”——小爱在回复你的同时也在持续倾听，你随时可以插话打断。说完它接着干，对话节奏更接近人与人之间的自然交流。

**********▍**************多轮对话****

一次长途出行，你可能和小爱聊了几十轮：先规划去露营地的路线，中途改目的地，又问了沿途天气，调了空调，最后让它推荐附近餐厅。每一轮对话都会把车内状态、工具调用、任务进度堆进上下文，Token 轻松突破十万级。

上下文越长，对模型的挑战越大——容易被无关信息带偏，响应速度也会变慢。**我们基于****Xiaomi MiMo****进一步优化，设计了三级 Session 压缩体系，给上下文进行“瘦身”**：

* **第一级，清掉过时状态。**空调温度、车窗开关这些信息每秒都在变，默认清空这些历史轮的快照。
* **第二级，只留当前任务相关的。**正在规划导航，之前聊音乐的就精简掉；太长就从最旧的删，最近几轮一定保住。
* **第三级，超长对话做摘要。**聊到上百轮时，把历史归纳成摘要，只留你的偏好这类长期有用的信息。

三级整理下来，上下文的 **Token****量下降 60%—86%**，而业务表现和合规率不降反升——就像一个记性好的副驾，不会因为聊了一路就忘了你最初要去哪，反而因为只记重点，回答得更专注、更准确。

**********▍**************打断接续能力****

打断，本来就是自然对话的一部分。人和人聊天时一句话被打断、稍后再补，大家都能自然接上。但过去的人机对话里，打断往往意味着上一件事就这么没了。

为了让打断后的交互更自然顺畅，小爱优化了打断接续的判断逻辑，区分不同场景精准处理，让判停更准确：

* **播报被打断：**如果只是播报类内容说了一半（如新闻、天气），信息已经完整，就不用接着往下念。
* **任务被打断：**如果正在执行的任务被打断（如导航还在规划），事情没做完，就会接着完成。
* **误打断：**如果是环境噪音导致的误触发，其实你没说话，它会自动回到刚才的任务上。
* **快抢慢重发：**如果新指令已经被快速响应，而旧的后台任务还在处理，会根据实际情况判断要不要继续。

判断的核心标准很简单：看最终交付的是「动作」还是「信息」。如果打断让你 “少做了一件事”，就继续做完；如果只是 “少听了一段话”，就到此为止。

你在表述时，它会结合语义完整性、说话节奏和对话上下文一起判断你是否说完，支持边想边说、中途自然停顿，小爱不会贸然抢话。播报过程中持续监听并识别有效人机请求，确认你是在对它说话后，就立刻停下播报、把话语权交还给你。而当你和同行人聊天、车内有噪音或咳嗽声时，它会安静地不打扰 —— 听得懂你什么时候在叫它，也分得清什么时候该安静。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=f68f90e8&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FrPSwicFZNl4bGDib9EDSslJMrvdVJsIic5ibiaW6RNRHugibkOOzN90sKMRpAacO2zj6kziaAwibHpTDQNuyictAQVMEUlGmjG88JOlbH1DC2QbAEhd4%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=ef54b02a&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2FrPSwicFZNl4aYHib00VPmUIBrvXsTtf8l4E6HzBNicWoqDcaEDNnFHYMlmphrXnoG8q7Z0HEicqhhRic2gKUPCSyXKOx49TGe6rcnPfibr9YagXyM%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg%26from%3Dappmsg)

它不只是空间可以变化，还能理解模糊语义，你说一句话，小爱就能懂你的场景、编排你的空间、执行你的需求。

超级小爱的升级，让简单指令能即刻响应，复杂需求也能又快又准地完成规划；对话也更加自然，你可以停顿、可以插话、可以想到哪说到哪，小爱像真人副驾一样接得住你的每一句话。

entries.title: 启动申报丨2026 CCF-快手大模型探索者基金
entries.content:
快手技术 2026-09-10 18:10 北京

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=fcecf90b&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2F1gVUsotpT1XItbeEiafCzeXjj1hrwoyMNYgaOV6KJyqC4DjKmeCEEcI5b2MaQ7kHoQe1StibAp2CR3CREkibCUHuYvlY83zE2jOLib0ssFvD7iak%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

5个研究方向，18个研究课题，25万元/课题，点击查看。

![图片](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=1bd5257e&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FZxDY5TMPs0EqL7dlyXD8OFyXn6yNGvQ8uEibL6TkOHqFvaK0bR9GEhZicTHuDtaTficMGS88ecXKIVPnFJCTMz7aQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg%26wxfrom%3D5%26wx_lazy%3D1%26tp%3Dwebp%23imgIndex%3D0)![](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=Mzg2NzU4MDM0MQ==&mid=2247501320&idx=1&sn=6c4198a4a72aa728ecea9b290eb12379)![](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=Mzg2NzU4MDM0MQ==&mid=2247501320&idx=1&sn=6c4198a4a72aa728ecea9b290eb12379)![](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=Mzg2NzU4MDM0MQ==&mid=2247501320&idx=1&sn=6c4198a4a72aa728ecea9b290eb12379)

CCF 与快手联合发布第三期"CCF-快手大模型探索者基金"（以下简称"大模型探索者基金"）并启动申报，面向全球大模型领域的优秀学者发布5个研究方向，共 18 项研究课题，每项课题提供人民币 25 万元的资助。申报截止时间：2026 年 10 月 7 日 24:00（北京时间），欢迎海内外学者积极申报。

2026 年 9 月，CCF 与快手联合发布第三期"CCF-快手大模型探索者基金"。本年度基金项目将延续聚焦于大模型技术基础研究与应用探索，加速技术成果产业化转化；同时致力于培养该领域科研与工程人才，通过搭建全球学者产学研合作平台，促进学术界与工业界深度交流合作，助力科技进步与社会发展。

大模型探索者基金在 2026 年度共发布 18 项研究课题，围绕"智能体(Agent)与自主进化"、"多模态大模型理解与生成"、"大模型安全与可信治理"、"大模型训练与推理优化"、"数据科学与实验科学"这 5 个重点研究方向，为每项课题提供人民币 25 万元的资助，同时快手将提供技术、算力、和脱敏数据等资源支持。项目期间，为确保学生能够接触到真实的应用场景，快手将提供学生实习的机会，实习生薪酬由快手公司单独承担。

「2026年度大模型探索者基金课题方向」

方向一、智能体(Agent)与自主进化

1.1 面向用户兴趣的端到端个性化短视频生成智能体研究

1.2 层次化递归自我改进框架优化通用智能体

1.3 基于 Rubric 驱动 Agentic RL 的电商多轮对话式导购 Agent

1.4 面向动态环境的下一代交互式智能体技术研究

1.5 基于多模态 Agent 的短视频深度理解技术研究

1.6 意图驱动的全链路音视频生产多智能体协同

1.7 Agent 上下文工程：面向多步骤任务的上下文压缩与卸载技术研究

方向二、多模态大模型理解与生成

2.1 面向视频理解的多模态大模型时序感知关键技术研究与应用

2.2 面向电商广告短视频 AIGC 的可交互数字商品和数字人生成

2.3 电商统一多模态基座及其 Agent 化能力供给

2.4 面向生服线索广告的异构序列多模态 Diffusion 长序列建模研究

方向三、大模型安全与可信治理

3.1 基于多模态大模型的视频内容风险细粒度定位与证据推理

3.2 面向安全治理的多模态内容理解大模型鲁棒学习方法研究

3.3 重构电商治理大模型增长范式：数据智能底座、可信评测体系与自进化后训练关键技术研究

方向四、大模型训练与推理优化

4.1 面向复杂交互与投机生成负载的大模型推理优化

4.2 时空语义理解驱动的智能视频编解码

4.3 面向垂直场景的大模型精调数据提纯与训练策略研究

方向五、数据科学与实验科学

5.1 双边问题实验设计与 AI 辅助因果估计方法研究

「申请条件」

本基金将面向符合如下条件的海内外所有高校及科研院所学者展开：

1、申请者须是全球高校/科研院所在职的全职教师或研究人员；

2、申请者具有博士学位或者研究生指导资格；

3、申请者能独立进行研究工作，并带领学生团队共同参与课题研究与实践；

「如何申报」

申请时间：

2026 年 9 月 2 日 18:00-2026 年 10 月 7 日  24:00（北京时间）

申请方式：

申请者点击"阅读原文"查看《2026年度CCF-快手大模型探索者基金课题介绍》，并下载、填写《CCF-快手大模型探索者基金2026年项目申报表》后提交至 IACF 数字化管理系统。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=10723e3b&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2F3nWJ62V5zdk5pic4ulXvtkySyTnW5cX08xbbujacVWfIE6lVxqGPGhxuFDrzzmSBnhatRZccWk8o9TnSaeOmPb1G6MkkeSug0OJIYpnwZVFc%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg%23imgIndex%3D0)

「基金评审」

CCF 和快手将共同邀请来自学界、业界的专家担任项目评委并组成项目专家组，共同评审并决定基金最终的资助结果以及资助额度。专家评审主要依据以下标准：

* 申请课题的作用、意义、创新性和可行性；
* 申请者的实施计划及输出成果的意义和价值；
* 申请者（及团队）的学术水平和科研能力；
* 研究计划与快手相关课题需求的匹配度。

「基金课题宣讲会」

针对本期 18 项课题，CCF 联合快手技术专家通过 CCF 视频号在线直播进行课题解析及答疑交流，可扫描直播二维码预约观看。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=cf1bc0e6&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2F3nWJ62V5zdlEgFsj7faA3cNmwa7B8qUjzMv85VrhaGy9V2RPKcgNKHdaBe9kRNfibCq8X1sdJl1msn1ZuyJ1hDm1pXqGf6hCMCo0vQibnKtQU%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg%26from%3Dappmsg%23imgIndex%3D1)

欢迎感兴趣的优秀学者积极申报，与快手携手推动大模型技术的边界拓展与深度研究，共同探索 AI 世界的无限可能。如您有任何问题或建议，欢迎邮件联系explorer\_fund@kuaishou.com，并在标题注明相关情况。

entries.title: 理想汽车将参加 2026 巴黎车展，i6 以“Li 6”之名首次面向欧洲公众展示
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，理想汽车今天（10 日）晚间宣布，在 9 月 7 日至 13 日举行的荷兰 2026 年索尔海姆杯高尔夫赛事期间，理想汽车将作为官方合作伙伴，为球员及 VIP 贵宾提供官方礼宾用车服务。

这是理想汽车正式启动进军欧洲的第一步。随后，理想汽车还将于 **2026 年 10 月**在巴黎车展完成欧洲车展首秀，向欧洲公众首次展示理想 i6（IT之家注：海外命名为 Li 6），届时理想汽车将公布全球产品阵容及欧洲业务计划。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/44825736-6ae3-4279-8bf6-b1c02618b1ba.png)

今年 5 月，理想汽车执行董事兼总裁马东辉透露了公司的国际化战略：海外市场主要采取分阶段拓展思路，结合当地市场规模和竞争格局，会灵活选用**设立子公司、发展经销商，或签约独家总代**等多种模式，并希望依托当地头部合作伙伴快速去搭建销售、交付、售后一体的完整服务体系。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/295fb6ed-0181-44a7-a919-474896da4d32.png)

具体市场布局方面，理想汽车计划 5 月陆续进入中国澳门、柬埔寨、老挝、缅甸；中东、中亚等市场以 L 系列增程车型为主力，全新 L9 将针对当地使用场景在**充电性能、座舱空调热管理**等软硬件层面进行优化，产品今年 Q3 登陆；欧洲市场方面，下半年会推出纯电车型 i6；针对右舵市场，年底会在**中国香港、新加坡等亚太核心区域**投放 MEGA 的右舵版本。

entries.title: NASA 与 IBM 联合发布开源月球研究基础大模型，可识别月表冰区与撞击坑
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 10 日消息，今年春天，NASA 的阿尔忒弥斯 2 号任务完成了具有历史意义的月球掠飞，这是 1972 年之后人类首次载人绕月飞行。4 月 6 日，宇航员里德 · 怀斯曼、克里斯蒂娜 · 科赫、维克多 · 格洛弗与杰里米 · 汉森抵达了比以往任何人都更远的地外空间。如今，NASA 在筹备后续阿尔忒弥斯系列任务的同时，正与 IBM 合作，为科研人员打造全新的月球研究工具。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/cb5d7c59-22b7-44c4-bef3-6d16ae740455.jpg)

当地时间周四，双方联合发布了 NASA-IBM 月球基础大模型。这是一套开源人工智能系统，可在 Hugging Face 平台下载。IBM 欧洲、英国及爱尔兰研究院院长胡安 · 贝尔纳韦-莫雷诺博士介绍，作为基础大模型，它可以完成多项任务。首先，NASA 与 IBM 发现，该模型特别擅长识别月球表面可能存在冰的区域。

IT之家注意到，双方开展了一项对照测试：将模型的预测结果，和一套依靠成熟科研流程生成的月球地图进行比对，这套地图融合了地形、温度以及其他环境数据。研究团队还把该模型和微软开发的高分辨率图像视觉处理模型 SwinV2-B 做对比，最终 NASA-IBM 模型的识别误差降低了 23%。之所以选用 SwinV2-B 作为参照，是因为它常被用作各类图像分析任务的基准模型。

NASA 和 IBM 还测试了模型识别、分类陨石坑的能力。在这项测试中，新模型仅使用一半训练数据，性能就比 SwinV2-B 高出 19%。8 月 5 日，SpaceX 一枚猎鹰 9 号火箭撞击月球，研究团队借此机会验证了模型能力。IBM 将撞击影像输入模型后，模型准确识别出撞击形成的新陨石坑，即便这个新坑和原有陨石坑大面积重叠。贝尔纳韦-莫雷诺评价：“效果非常出色，模型一次就识别成功。”

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/b8c9b3dd-5d11-4e38-b3a5-e5e601e00ac2.jpg)

贝尔纳韦-莫雷诺表示，训练这套模型本身就充满挑战。他解释道：“在地球遥感观测中，我们能拿到画质完好的图像。地球大气会散射阳光，环境光可以填充阴影区域，让阴影边缘变得柔和。但月球上的阴影边缘锐利如刀，漆黑一片。拍摄时，阴影区域的像素不携带任何有效信息。”他说：“月球上，不同时段的阳光照射角度不同，时而照亮地表，时而划出浓重阴影，模型必须处理这类光影变化。同一个陨石坑，在不同照片里看起来可能完全不一样。”

另一个难题来自计算机视觉模型常规的训练与测试逻辑。常规做法一般是抹除图像的部分区域，让模型基于训练学到的图像规律，还原被抹掉的内容。贝尔纳韦-莫雷诺举例：“我们可以抹掉一个陨石坑 90% 的画面，只留下 10%，让模型还原剩下 90%。”这套方法放到月球场景行不通。原因不难理解：从轨道拍摄的照片里，大量陨石坑外观高度相似。

贝尔纳韦-莫雷诺称，IBM 一开始尝试用传统方式训练模型，结果“完全失败”。研究团队最终想出了一套创新方案：“我们把月球像橙子一样切成多个扇形区块，训练集区块和测试集区块完全分开。这样一来，模型训练就能保持良好的一致性。”

NASA 与 IBM 对这次发布寄予厚望，其中一个重要原因是配套推出了全球首个同类开源数据集，可供其他科研人员用来开发新模型。数据集整合了数万张影像与探测仪器数据，来源包括 NASA 的月球勘测轨道飞行器（LRO）、重力恢复与内部实验室（GRAIL）任务，以及日本的月亮女神号月球探测器（SELENE）。

贝尔纳韦-莫雷诺说：“过去一直没有功能全面、性能强大的月球专用大模型，一大原因就是缺少整理得当的配套数据。”这里的数据整理，指构建一套网格体系，让影像里每一个像素，都能对应模型可调用的其他维度探测数据。“单单这件事本身就是重大科研成果。抛开模型不谈，科研圈现在拥有了一套配准对齐的数据集，包含超过 200 万个数据点。”他补充道：“AI 模型总会被更新的模型淘汰，但数据才是支撑 AI 模型持续发展的根基。”
entries.summary: NASA与IBM联合开源月球基础大模型及包含超200万数据点的配准数据集，识别误差较基准降低23%。

entries.title: Show HN: AI Brand Visibility for Free Forever
entries.content:
Suppose you have a brand you care about — your own business or a nice business you are a fan of. I built a thing which lets you see what shows up in LLM searches and you can send it to my servers for comprehensive analysis, all completely free forever with beautiful dashboards and such!

The reason I built it is that I make my purchase decisions with LLMs (I don't delegate all my life to them \_yet\_), since 2023. As you can imagine, there was *a lot of hallucinations*, so I got obssessed for a while with how to make sure that the LLMs respond about brands with facts.

I was triggered a lot by wrappers that were charging money for API calls, so I decided to build it properly and hand over the keys to whoever wants to use it. With geoSurge you connect your existing LLM subscriptions to gather LLM sentiment, you use your spare tokens so it doesn't cost you anything in usage. After you get the data, you can look at the outputs or get geoSurge sentiment analysis for free.

My gf is using it to monitor her Japanese baking class studio: <https://okashi-school.com>.

---

entries.title: fix: keep thinking choices tied to the selected model (#142822)
entries.content:
```
fix: keep thinking choices tied to the selected model (#142822)

Related: #136257

## What changes

Keep model and provider together when the Control UI resolves a thinking profile. A partial session identity cannot borrow its missing half from defaults. New Session forwards the same resolved target. The redundant mixed-identity helper is removed.

Keep a saved Off override in the selector descriptor when the profile has no choices. The existing non-reasoning, nonempty Off-only display exception remains. No slider stop or implicit setting write is added. Production code changes by 12 additions and 18 deletions across two files.

Ayaan explicitly accepts the partial model/provider cleanup as an internal invariant refactor. It does not claim to fix a reachable runtime bug, and a supported producer of the synthetic partial tuple is not required solely to justify this accepted internal cleanup. Internal source and consumer regression evidence establishes that scope. Ordinary same-version Gateway session and agent producers publish complete identity pairs. The saved-Off lifecycle remains the separately proved public outcome; correctness, security, CI and all other proof gates remain.

## Evidence

- Four baseline selector/consumer failures at `3f0f98ef7efe3c3fceb180b9bef908de5792c7b4` and 28 affected candidate passes cover the original contracts and preservation controls. Their full source, commands and results remain retained.
- A real Gateway lifecycle now supplies the saved-Off/empty-profile input: create a session with the short `with-effort` reference, save Off while supported, then use `/model thinking-fixture/no-effort`. Public responses resolve the short reference to a complete identity and retain Off after the profile becomes empty. The session-change event carries both model and provider while omitting the profile.
- The actual browser shows `Current thinking level: off.` and `Options: none.`, adds no slider, refuses High and leaves the saved value unchanged. Its complete capture contains six CLI calls and 113 non-authentication WebSocket frames. The sole browser setting write changes the model; no `chat.send` or unintended thinking patch occurs.
- The new real-Gateway case passed in 8.584 seconds in [job 102857642159](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34473103003/job/102857642159), at `f5a9412eac074626ceb8d46c9a92798c5c091935`. [The public proof artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34473103003/artifacts/10150867398) includes the complete observations and screenshot. The existing no-override control also passed.
- `405bd88f4e0ec605a067b2b7172f5b8416e259c3` separates the recorder's two event registrations to fix the generated TypeScript overload error. Its production code, scenario actions, filtering and assertions are unchanged. [Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34475274851) checks that exact corrected head.

## Limits and preserved behavior

The real-Gateway case proves admission, readback and visible lifecycle behavior. Its unchanged `/think` reader does not independently demonstrate the hidden selector descriptor repair. That distinction is covered by the original source assertions and remains for code-aware review. The observed complete identities do not establish a universal impossibility of partial inputs.

Earlier Chromium evidence used a maintained synthetic Gateway. Its two reporter emissions are one 34-request case; the prior independent acceptance remains limited to those synthetic observations. All three earlier blocked local reviews, the bounded native lint failure, the public scan deadline, the corrected type error and earlier Chromium connection timeout remain retained. The owner's new internal-refactor approval changes the next review input; it does not edit or reuse an earlier verdict. Fresh exact-head review is required. Current CI passes type checking and the real-Gateway browser job; its remaining docs-navigation and managed-child tooling failures require causal disposition before landing.

Complete identities, matching runtime profiles, inherited choices, unknown-support server validation, draft reconciliation and Fast reset retain their current contracts. Native profile producers and provider-login work remain separate.

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>
```

entries.title: Max Brooks reflects on 20 years of ‘World War Z’
entries.content:
A new virus emerges in rural China. Although those who contract it initially display moderate, flu-like symptoms, their health quickly declines. The mortality rate is unclear, but one aspect is immediately obvious—it’s very contagious. Within three months, nations around the world are planning lockdown protocols and quarantine measures. Politicians seem completely out of their league and ill-equipped.

The world eventually recovers from the ordeal, but consequences of the virus linger for decades.While society pushes forward, there’s no promise that an even deadlier virus isn’t already lurking out of sight.

This isn’t about COVID-19, by the way. It’s the plot to the novel *World War Z*—arguably the most realistic depiction of a zombie apocalypse ever created. Released 20 years ago this week, the horror novel by [Max Brooks](https://www.maxbrooks.com/) quickly became one of the undisputed cornerstones of walking dead canon. Readers and critics devoured the book (no pun intended), but their responses often worry Brooks. Much like the reception to his first book, [*The Zombie Survival Guide*](http://links.penguinrandomhouse.com/type/affiliate/isbn/9781400049622/siteID/8001/retailerid/6/trackingcode/penguinrandom), many fans seem to misunderstand his intentions. These projects weren’t simply intended to entertain. Max Brooks was trying to warn everyone about the looming threats we would prefer to ignore.

While the 54-year-old writer ostensibly writes books about zombies, Sasquatch, and (soon) an alien invasion, his attention to disaster details and hyperrealism has earned him a parallel career as a [security and threat analyst](https://www.atlanticcouncil.org/expert/max-brooks/) for some of the world’s most respected geopolitical think tanks.

To celebrate *World War Z*’s 20th anniversary, *Popular Science* recently spoke with Brooks about the book’s massive impact.

*This interview has been edited for length and clarity.*

![Max Brooks attends the "World War Z" premiere in Times Square in New York City. © LAN](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Max-Brooks-WWZ-Premiere.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

*Max Brooks attends the* World War Z *movie premiere in Times Square in New York City on June 17, 2013. Credit: [LAN via Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/max-brooks-attends-the-world-war-z-premiere-in-times-square-news-photo/526329286?adppopup=true)* © LAN

**Andrew Paul: Did you anticipate *World War Z* attaining the legacy it now has in popular culture?**

**Max Brooks:** Oh, God no. Of course not. Especially because I’m never tapped into pop culture. I don’t know what anybody else is doing—even when it was my job writing for [*Saturday Night Live*](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0112150/bio/)! I’m good at thinking about what I think about.

**AP: Before *World War Z*, you wrote an actual preparedness handbook called *The Zombie Survival Guide*. What prompted you to take a hyperreal approach to such a seemingly outlandish subject?**

**MB:** The reason I wrote [them] was because all the zombie stories, even to this day, tend to focus around small groups. To me, it’s like trying to understand World War II from watching *Saving Private Ryan*. I had big picture questions nobody was answering.

I think the best zombie movie ever made was *Dawn of the Dead*. To me, the most interesting part was when they’re holed up in the mall watching the news. That window into the wider world was so fascinating, and I wanted more.

**AP: But there was a time when *World War Z* almost never happened, right?**

**MB:** [The publisher] didn’t know what to do with *The Zombie Survival Guide.* Their marketing strategy almost killed my career before it even launched. They thought, “Well, no one is clearly that much of a loser that he’s actually spent this much time thinking about [zombies]. Clearly, he’s a cool guy making fun of those losers. And because he’s Mel Brooks’ son and he’s coming off *SNL*, we’re gonna position him as Mel Brooks, Jr. writing *Younger Frankenstein*.”

But *The Zombie Survival Guide* really is a disaster preparedness manual. It’s why [soldiers] took it to Afghanistan; people told me it saved their lives when they were lost in the woods. I didn’t make anything up. It’s not Hollywood stuff—it’s all about dehydration and dry socks and shelter.

But [these books were] legitimately the product of years of thinking, “If I was in a zombie world, how would I survive?”It really set me on this path of asking, “What happens when the grown-ups drop the ball?”

**AP: And now it’s your job to worry professionally.**

**MB:** I’ve now been part of three military and national security think tanks—the Atlantic Council, the Center for Strategic and International Studies, and the Modern War Institute at West Point. I’m a non-resident senior fellow at all three of them, and it’s my job to study real threats.

For some reason, I was not blessed with the wall of denial. Like, I can’t just say, “That would *never* happen and I’m just going to go about my merry way.” I’m already terrified! And the way to reduce my anxiety is to study the threat so that it’s not nebulous.

**AP: What was the most difficult part in preparing to write *World War Z*?**

**MB:** You don’t know what you don’t know, so you don’t know what you’re missing. There’s always a fear of groping around in the dark; of not even knowing who to talk to. That was a real struggle, because I’m an insular guy. I’m not a social guy. Part of it was talking to experts, but part of it was reading books—and I’m fully dyslexic. So that was a real slog.

It was also about never trusting the internet. I used it once or twice, like, to research laser weaponry. I literally went to a company’s website, saw their demonstration video, and was like, “Yeah, okay. That is not a practical weapon for hunting zombies. I see how long it takes to burn through something.”

![NEW YORK - JULY 25: The Late Show with Stephen Colbert and guest Max Brooks during Tuesday's July 25 2017 show. (Photo by Scott Kowalchyk/CBS via Getty Images)](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Max-Brooks-Colbert.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

*Stephen Colbert described Brooks as the ‘zombie laureate’ in 2017. Credit: [Scott Kowalchyk/CBS via Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/the-late-show-with-stephen-colbert-and-guest-max-brooks-news-photo/823527210?adppopup=true)* CBS Photo Archive

**AP: Obviously humanity’s most terrifying challenge in the last 20 years was the COVID-19 pandemic. How do you view that real-world horror in the context of *World War Z*?**

**MB:** COVID was scary because I knew it was coming thanks to my friends in the military and biodefense community. I was part of what was called the [Blue Ribbon Biodefense Panel](https://biodefensecommission.org/) for germ attacks way before COVID. So I already had at my fingertips the ability to tell the difference between panic porn in the media and the real deal. I also had to study diseases enough to write about a zombie plague. But also, it came from being on the receiving end of a bioterror attack. When I worked at *SNL* [from 2001 to 2003], we had the anthrax letters delivered to our building [in October 2001].

So, I knew this was coming, but the question was how to warn people. I had people laughing at me. Ironically, the people who are the worst minds to reach are the smarty-smarts because they think they know everything.

**AP: Were you expecting COVID to be much worse than it was?**

**MB:** Oh, much worse. It got me into trouble, because I was prepping for, like, tanks on the street, you know? I was ready for that. I stocked my home with food that would last the longest as opposed to food that my wife would actually eat.

But the irony is, had it been worse, we might have actually done better. Studying diseases over the years—it’s sort of like the slow zombie versus the fast zombie. The fast zombie is so scary you have to react. The slow zombie gives you the false sense of security. Like, “Oh, I can take ‘em out.” COVID was the slow zombie. It allowed us to be arrogant and dismiss it: “Oh, it’s no worse than the flu.”

**AP: How did you see that play out during the quarantine?**

**MB:** It goes back to when COVID hit New York City. I had written a book called *The Harlem Hellfighters*, which was a true story of African American soldiers in World War I. They’re still an active unit in the National Guard, and I’m friends with their chief medical officer. Their job was to pick up the dead bodies around New York.

He said to me, “If those bodies had been stacked up on the street for everyone to see them, there would have been no argument about masking or distancing or taking the vaccine.” The hiding of it is what allowed naysayers to get way more people killed.

**AP: Where did the grown-ups “drop the ball,” as you say?**

**MB:** I think the greatest failure on the part of leadership at every level was not publicizing the dead. Maybe they were afraid of angry letters and backlash and didn’t want to cause a panic, but that’s exactly what they should have done.

A doctor in Los Angeles told me they converted hospital rooms into morgues. He said, “You don’t believe the amount of bodies. We’ve got pyramids of body bags.” And I’m like, “Well, then why is this not on the news every night?”

**AP: After experiencing an actual global plague, how do you feel about *World War Z*’s overall accuracy?**

**MB:** I think it was accurate for the time. I would still have the plague coming from China, 100 percent. I would love to say that was my genius futuristic prediction, but no. I based it on SARS. And this is why it’s unforgivable that it happened again. If I wrote it today, I would really highlight why it was allowed to be [downplayed]—and the reason is our greed. All of our stuff is made in China.

I would also really change the politicization of information. We’re living in a time where all facts have become tribalized. We’ve had 20 years of such dumbing down that I think it would be a central tenant of the book.

**AP: Would you change how the United States responded to a zombie outbreak?**

**MB:** I still firmly believe we are a moderate country, but I don’t know how brave we are. In order for a crime to be committed, you don’t need 100 bullies. You just need one bully and 99 cowards.

The psycho fanatics have a microphone now, which was inconceivable 20 years ago. They are hate merchants, and the erosion of our education system has created a demand that the merchants supply.

**AP: So you think we would have handled COVID differently in 2006?**

**MB:** If COVID happened 20 years earlier, we would all have gotten vaccinated, because of all the grandmas and grandpas who grew up before the polio vaccine.

**AP: What else has changed?**

**MB:** When I talk to people in power, I try to educate them about what I call “uphill influence” versus “downhill influence.” Downhill influence is when there’s a pre-existing bias that you just need to hijack and ride downhill. There’s gravity already there, and that’s not necessarily a bad thing. It was an established fact 20 or 30 years ago that vaccines kept you safe. So, if you were rolling out a vaccine, you could already just ride that existence acceptance downhill. The gravity was with you.

Uphill is when you have to educate before you can even start to persuade. You first have to educate people about just the world that you’re trying to explain. Vaccines have gone from downhill to uphill. The [subjects] we all had to try to stay awake through in seventh grade science class aren’t even there anymore.

I understand [MAHA supporters] want a clean planet, food, and water, and all of that will make you healthier. However, in 1491, the people who lived on this continent had all that, right? The moment the first Javier Bardem-looking Spaniard coughed on them, whole civilizations died.

![Max Brooks and Mel Brooks at the Los Angeles premiere of HBO Documentary Films' "Mel Brooks: 99 Year Old Man!" held at the Tedd Mann Theater at The Academy Museum on January 20, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Chad Salvador/Variety via Getty Images)](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Max-Mel-Brooks.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

*Max Brooks and Mel Brooks at the Los Angeles premiere of HBO Documentary Films’* Mel Brooks: 99 Year Old Man! *on January 20, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Credit: [Chad Salvador/Variety via Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/max-brooks-and-mel-brooks-at-the-los-angeles-premiere-of-news-photo/2256790647?adppopup=true)* Chad Salvador

**AP: Both of your zombie books hinge on public education, and that’s now a major aspect of your threat analysis work. Do you know why you keep returning to this theme?**

**MB:** I think one of the reasons I’m so obsessed with education is because I was not a good student. I have such ferocious learning disabilities. I never felt instantly comfortable learning, and I’ve always had to find workarounds. My mother had to help me find workarounds so I could learn. So when I research, it takes so much time and effort and [there’s] so much insecurity. I understand how hard it is to teach something to someone who doesn’t naturally pick it up.

I’m very lucky that I come from two parents who had no formal education, but were both very smart. Most importantly, they were very curious. I became very comfortable with the idea of approaching something as an absolute beginner.

**AP: It took 14 years between *World War Z* and your follow-up sci-fi novel, *Devolution*. Your next book, [*The First Hundred Hours: A Story of Alien Invasion*](https://www.maxbrooks.com/news/2026/1/28/a-new-story-for-a-new-world-an-excerpt-introduction-from-max-brooks), comes out in 2027. Is there a reason for such long pauses between these projects?**

**MB:** I’m not a natural scientist. The amount I’ve had to study for this new book has been excruciating. But it’s very humbling having to talk to the experts and say things like, “Please talk to me like I’m a third grader—and not a smart third grader.”

**AP: Would you end *World War Z* the same if it was set in 2026?**

**MB:** I would still end it on a positive note, and I think that has to do with being an American. We don’t have the luxury of abandoning our ideals, because that’s all we are. We’re not a nation-state—the ideals in America are all that hold this mutt [of a] nation together. We all come from different places and tribes, and we all agree to live under a certain set of guidelines. It’s really critical that we fight for those guidelines.

If there is one takeaway, it’s the central reason I wrote the book in the first place. We’re all stuck on the same planet together, and that planet is not that big anymore. What affects some of us could potentially affect all of us. I think America has some amazing cultural strengths, but one of our weaknesses is our isolationism. That’s built on an outdated notion that we are somehow protected by two oceans and our geography. That’s not true anymore.

The post [Max Brooks reflects on 20 years of ‘World War Z’](https://www.popsci.com/science/max-brooks-world-war-z-interview/) appeared first on [Popular Science](https://www.popsci.com).
